sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__

translations.literal: Table of contents.
translations.idiomatic: Table of contents.

sentences.zh: 有明諸籓，分封而不錫土，列爵而不臨民，食祿而不治事，史稱其制善。

translations.literal: Under the Ming, the enfeoffed princes were granted titles but not fiefs, given ranks but did not govern the people, received stipends but did not administer affairs; historians praised this system as sound.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ming, imperial clansmen were enfeoffed without receiving territorial fiefs, granted noble ranks without governing commoners, and drew stipends without holding administrative duties; the histories call this arrangement a good one.

sentences.zh: 清興，諸子弟但稱台吉、貝勒；

translations.literal: When the Qing arose, the imperial sons and younger brothers were styled only taiji and beile;
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Qing, the emperor's sons and brothers bore only the titles taiji and beile;

sentences.zh: 既乃斅明建親、郡王，而次以貝勒、貝子，又次以公爵，復別為不入八分。

translations.literal: Thereafter they followed the Ming model of enfeoffing kinsmen as princes, and next came beile and beizi, then dukes, with a further category excluded from the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Later they adopted the Ming practice of enfeoffing imperial kinsmen as princes, followed in rank by beile and beizi, then dukes, and finally a separate class not admitted to the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 蓋所以存國俗，而等殺既多，屏衛亦益廣，下此則有將軍，無中尉，又與明小異；

translations.literal: This was meant to preserve national custom; yet with so many gradations of rank, the protective screen of the dynasty also grew broader. Below these there were generals but no commandery princes, differing slightly from the Ming again;
translations.idiomatic: The design preserved Manchu custom while multiplying ranks so that the dynasty's bulwark grew wider still. Beneath these ranks stood generals but not commandery princes—a further slight departure from Ming practice;

sentences.zh: 諸王不錫土，而其封號但予嘉名，不加郡國，視明為尤善。

translations.literal: the princes received no fiefs, and their titles were only honorific names, without attachment to commanderies or states—regarded as even better than under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Qing princes likewise received no territorial fiefs; their titles were purely honorific, without appanage to a commandery or state, which was judged superior even to the Ming system.

sentences.zh: 然內襄政本，外領師幹，與明所謂不臨民、不治事者乃絕相反。

translations.literal: Yet they took part in the core of government within and commanded armies without—utterly unlike what the Ming called not governing the people and not administering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within the court they shared in the foundations of government, and without they led armies—precisely the opposite of the Ming ideal of princes who neither governed the people nor handled affairs.

sentences.zh: 國初開創，櫛風沐雨，以百戰定天下，繄諸王是庸。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, braving wind and rain, the realm was settled through a hundred battles, and it was through the princes that this was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's founding years, the emperors endured hardship and won the empire in a century of warfare, relying above all on the princes.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，出討三籓，勝負互見，而卒底蕩平之績。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign they marched out against the Three Feudatories; victories and defeats alternated, yet in the end they achieved complete pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi they campaigned against the Three Feudatories; though fortune seesawed, they ultimately brought the rebellion to a full end.

sentences.zh: 其後行師西北，仍以諸王典兵。

translations.literal: Afterward, when armies were sent to the northwest, princes again held command.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigns in the northwest were again entrusted to princes as commanders.

sentences.zh: 雍正、乾隆諒闇之始，重臣宅揆，亦領以諸王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongzheng and Qianlong reigns, when senior ministers held the chief ministership, princes also headed those posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Yongzheng and Qianlong reigns, when great ministers held the premiership, princes likewise led those offices.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，以親王為軍機大臣，未幾，以非祖制罷。

translations.literal: Early in the Jiaqing reign a prince was made a Grand Councilor; before long he was removed as contrary to ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing a prince was appointed to the Grand Council, but soon removed because the appointment violated ancestral precedent.

sentences.zh: 穆宗踐阼，輟贊襄之命，而設議政王，尋仍改直樞廷。

translations.literal: When the Tongzhi Emperor ascended the throne, the office of assisting the throne was suspended and a Prince Regent was appointed; soon the Grand Council was restored in its direct form.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongzhi came to the throne, the mandate to assist the ruler was set aside and a Prince Regent was installed; shortly afterward government reverted to the direct Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 自是相沿，爰及季年，親貴用事，以攝政始，以攝政終。

translations.literal: From then on, down to the dynasty's last years, the imperial kin held power—beginning with regency and ending with regency.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, down to the dynasty's closing years, the imperial clan wielded authority—rule began under a regent and ended under one.

sentences.zh: 論者謂有天焉，誠一代得失之林也。

translations.literal: Commentators say this was Heaven's doing; truly it is a forest of gains and losses for an entire age.
translations.idiomatic: Observers called this the working of Heaven; in truth it forms a whole thicket of what one age gained and lost.

sentences.zh: 今用諸史例，以皇子為宗，子孫襲爵者從焉；

translations.literal: Now, following the examples of the various histories, those taken as the imperial line are the sons of emperors, and those descendants who inherit noble ranks are included;
translations.idiomatic: Here, following precedent in the various histories, imperial sons form the main line, and descendants who inherit noble titles are included as well;

sentences.zh: 子孫別有功績復立爵者亦從焉。

translations.literal: descendants who separately achieved merit and were again ennobled are also included.
translations.idiomatic: so too are descendants who later won distinction and received new enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 其爵世，備書之；

translations.literal: Where titles pass from generation to generation, full accounts are given;
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary titles are recorded in full;

sentences.zh: 其爵不世，則具詳於表。

translations.literal: where titles do not pass down, details are set out in the tables.
translations.idiomatic: non-hereditary ranks are given in detail in the tables.

sentences.zh: 表曰皇子，傳曰諸王，亦互文以見義焉。

translations.literal: The tables say "imperial sons," the biographies say "the various princes"—a deliberate interchange of terms to bring out the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The tables speak of "imperial sons" while the biographies speak of "the various princes"—a deliberate alternation of wording to clarify the distinction.

sentences.zh: 自公以下，別被除拜具有事實者，及疏宗登追列高位著名績者，皆散與諸臣相次。

translations.literal: From dukes downward, those separately enfeoffed or dismissed when there are concrete facts, and distant clansmen posthumously raised to high rank for noted achievements, are scattered among the various ministers in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: From the rank of duke downward, those separately enfeoffed or removed when facts warrant it, and collateral clansmen posthumously elevated for famous deeds, are interleaved in order among the other ministers.

sentences.zh: 清矯明失，宗子與庶姓並用，通前史之例以存其實也。

translations.literal: The Qing corrected Ming errors by employing imperial clansmen and commoners alike, following the precedent of earlier histories to preserve the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing corrected Ming mistakes by employing both imperial clansmen and commoners, following earlier historiographic practice to preserve what actually happened.

sentences.zh: 景祖五子：翼皇后生顯祖；

translations.literal: Emperor Jing had five sons: by Empress Yi he had Emperor Xian;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzu had five sons: by Empress Yi he fathered Emperor Xianzu;

sentences.zh: 諸子，武功郡王禮敦，慧哲郡王額爾袞，宣獻郡王齋堪，恪恭貝勒塔察篇古，皆不詳其母氏。

translations.literal: the other sons were Prince of Military Merit Li Dun, Prince of Sagacious Wisdom Ergun, Prince of Exalted Offering Zhaikan, and Prince of Reverent Respect Tachapiangu—all their mothers are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: His other sons were Li Dun, Prince of Military Merit; Ergun, Prince of Sagacious Wisdom; Zhaikan, Prince of Exalted Offering; and Tachapiangu, Prince of Reverent Respect—their mothers are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 武功郡王禮敦，景祖第一子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Military Merit Li Dun was the first son of Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dun, Prince of Military Merit, was the eldest son of Emperor Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 肇祖而下，世系始詳，事蹟未備，四傳至興祖。

translations.literal: From the Founding Ancestor downward the genealogy first becomes detailed, but deeds are not complete; four generations pass to Emperor Xing.
translations.idiomatic: From the Founding Ancestor the line becomes detailed, though deeds are still incomplete; four generations later came Emperor Xingzu.

sentences.zh: 興祖六子：長，德世庫；

translations.literal: Emperor Xing had six sons: the eldest, Deshiku;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xingzu had six sons: the eldest, Deshiku;

sentences.zh: 次，劉闡；

translations.literal: the second, Liuchan;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Liuchan;

sentences.zh: 次，索長阿；

translations.literal: the third, Suochang'a;
translations.idiomatic: the third, Suochang'a;

sentences.zh: 次，景祖；

translations.literal: the fourth, Emperor Jing;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth, Emperor Jingzu;

sentences.zh: 次，包朗阿；

translations.literal: the fifth, Baolang'a;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth, Baolang'a;

sentences.zh: 次，寶實：號「甯古塔貝勒」。

translations.literal: the sixth, Baoshi, styled the "Ningguta Beile."
translations.idiomatic: the sixth, Baoshi, known as the "Ningguta Beile."

sentences.zh: 景祖承肇祖舊業，居赫圖阿拉，德世庫居覺爾察，劉闡居阿哈河洛，索長阿居河洛噶善，包朗阿居尼麻喇，寶實居章甲，環赫圖阿拉而城，近者五里，遠者二十里，互相。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing inherited the Founding Ancestor's legacy and dwelt at Hetu Ala; Deshiku lived at Jue'ercha, Liuchan at Ahaheluo, Suochang'a at Heluogashan, Baolang'a at Nimara, and Baoshi at Zhangjia. They ringed Hetu Ala with settlements, the nearest five li away and the farthest twenty li, mutually supporting one another.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzu took over the Founding Ancestor's patrimony and resided at Hetu Ala. Deshiku lived at Jue'ercha, Liuchan at Ahaheluo, Suochang'a at Heluogashan, Baolang'a at Nimara, and Baoshi at Zhangjia. They built settlements around Hetu Ala, the nearest five li distant and the farthest twenty, lending one another mutual support.

sentences.zh: 寶實子阿哈納渥濟格與董鄂部長克轍巴顏有隙，屢來侵。

translations.literal: Baoshi's son Ahanawojige had a feud with Kezhebayan, chief of the Donggo tribe, who repeatedly came to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Baoshi's son Ahanawojige quarreled with Kezhebayan, chief of the Donggo tribe, who raided them again and again.

sentences.zh: 索長阿子吳泰，哈達萬汗婿也，乞援於哈達，攻董鄂部，取數寨，董鄂部兵乃不復至。

translations.literal: Suochang'a's son Wutai, son-in-law of Wan Khan of Hada, begged Hada for aid, attacked the Donggo tribe, and took several stockades, so Donggo troops came no more.
translations.idiomatic: Suochang'a's son Wutai, who had married a daughter of Wan Khan of Hada, sought Hada's help, attacked the Donggo, captured several forts, and Donggo forces ceased to appear.

sentences.zh: 「甯古塔」亦自此稍弱。

translations.literal: "Ningguta" also grew somewhat weaker from this.
translations.idiomatic: The "Ningguta" line likewise grew somewhat weaker from this point.

sentences.zh: 及太祖兵起，德世庫、劉闡、索長阿、寶實等子孫惎其英武，屢欲加害；

translations.literal: When the Taizu raised his army, the descendants of Deshiku, Liuchan, Suochang'a, Baoshi, and others envied his prowess and repeatedly tried to harm him;
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu raised his armies, the descendants of Deshiku, Liuchan, Suochang'a, Baoshi, and the rest envied his martial brilliance and more than once sought his life;

sentences.zh: 其後益強大，謀始戢。

translations.literal: afterward, as he grew ever stronger, their plots finally ceased.
translations.idiomatic: but as he grew ever stronger their schemes at last subsided.

sentences.zh: 索長阿、寶實子孫皆從攻戰，包朗阿雲孫拜山尤有功，自有傳。

translations.literal: The descendants of Suochang'a and Baoshi all followed him in campaigns; Baolang'a's great-grandson Baishan was especially meritorious and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of Suochang'a and Baoshi followed him in battle; Baolang'a's great-grandson Baishan distinguished himself especially and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 帝業既成，景祖諸兄弟追封皆未及。

translations.literal: After the imperial enterprise was achieved, posthumous enfeoffments for Emperor Jing's brothers were never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial enterprise was secured, Emperor Jingzu's brothers received no posthumous enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 禮敦生而英勇，景祖討平碩色納、奈呼二部，禮敦功最，號曰「巴圖魯」。

translations.literal: Li Dun was brave from birth. When Emperor Jing pacified the Shuosena and Naihu tribes, Li Dun's merit was greatest and he was styled "Baturu."
translations.idiomatic: Li Dun was valiant from youth. When Emperor Jingzu subdued the Shuosena and Naihu tribes, Li Dun's service stood foremost and he was hailed as "Baturu."

sentences.zh: 太祖兵起，禮敦卒久矣。

translations.literal: When the Taizu raised his army, Li Dun had long been dead.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Taizu took up arms, Li Dun had been dead for many years.

sentences.zh: 太祖既定東京，葬景祖、顯祖于楊魯山，以禮敦陪葬。

translations.literal: After the Taizu secured the Eastern Capital, he buried Emperors Jing and Xian at Yanglu Mountain and had Li Dun buried with them.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu secured the Eastern Capital he interred Emperors Jingzu and Xianzu at Yanglu Mountain and had Li Dun buried beside them.

sentences.zh: 崇德四年八月，進封武功郡王，配享太廟。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Chongde he was advanced to Prince of Military Merit and granted joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chongde 4 he was posthumously raised to Prince of Military Merit and granted joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 子貝和齊，太祖伐明，攻廣寧，留守遼陽。

translations.literal: His son Beiheqi, when the Taizu attacked the Ming and assaulted Guangning, remained to guard Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Beiheqi, when Taizu campaigned against the Ming and attacked Guangning, stayed behind to guard Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 孫色勒，事太祖，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: His grandson Sele served the Taizu and was appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Sele served Taizu and was appointed niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 事太宗，自十六大臣進八大臣，授正藍旗固山額真。

translations.literal: Serving the Taizong, he rose from among the Sixteen Ministers to the Eight Ministers and was appointed gushan ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he advanced from among the Sixteen Ministers to the Eight Ministers and was made gushan ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 從太宗圍大淩河，軍城南，屢擊敗明兵。

translations.literal: He followed the Taizong in besieging Dalinghe, encamped south of the city, and repeatedly defeated Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong in the siege of Dalinghe, encamped south of the city, and repeatedly routed Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗略宣府、大同，與貝勒德格類入獨石口，敗明兵于長安嶺，攻赤城，克其郛。

translations.literal: He again followed the Taizong in raiding Xuanfu and Datong, and with Prince Degui entered Dushikou, defeated Ming troops at Chang'an Ridge, attacked Chicheng, and captured its outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Taizong in raids on Xuanfu and Datong, and with Prince Degui entered Dushikou, defeated Ming troops at Chang'an Ridge, attacked Chicheng, and took its outer suburbs.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事，降鑲黃旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for an offense he was demoted to meiren ejen of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, for an offense he was demoted to meiren ejen of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 崇德初，從伐朝鮮，朝鮮國王李倧遣妻子入江華島，走保南漢山城。

translations.literal: Early in Chongde he followed the campaign against Korea. King Li Jong of Korea sent his wife and children to Jianghua Island and took refuge in Namhansanseong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongde he joined the Korean campaign. King Li Jong sent his wife and children to Jianghua Island and held out in Namhansanseong.

sentences.zh: 豫親王多鐸圍之急，朝鮮將赴援，色勒與甲喇額真阿爾津擊敗之。

translations.literal: Prince Dorgon pressed the siege hard; when Korean forces came to relieve the city, Sele and jalan ejen Arjin defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dorgon pressed the siege hard; when Korean relief forces approached, Sele and jalan ejen Arjin defeated them.

sentences.zh: 分兵攻江華島，色勒率右翼兵渡海，越敵艦，近躍登島，破其守兵，得倧妻子。

translations.literal: Forces were divided to attack Jianghua Island; Sele led the right wing across the sea, leaped over enemy ships, boarded the island at close range, broke the defenders, and captured Jong's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were split to attack Jianghua Island; Sele led the right wing across the sea, sprang over enemy vessels, boarded the island at close quarters, routed the garrison, and seized Jong's family.

sentences.zh: 倧既降，論功，授牛錄章京世職，兼吏部右參政。

translations.literal: After Jong surrendered, for merit he was granted the hereditary office of niru janggin and concurrently made right vice-president of the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Jong submitted, Sele was rewarded with the hereditary office of niru janggin and concurrently appointed right vice-president of the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，擢內大臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was promoted to inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he was promoted to inner minister.

sentences.zh: 錄禮敦諸孫席賚、阿濟賚、阿賚等，並授拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: Li Dun's grandsons Xisai, Ajisai, Asai, and others were all granted the rank of baitalaburu hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dun's grandsons Xisai, Ajisai, Asai, and others were all granted the rank of baitalaburu hafan.

sentences.zh: 色勒進一等阿思哈尼哈番，再進二等精奇尼哈番，擢領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: Sele was advanced to first-class ashan i hafan, then to second-class jingkini hafan, and promoted to leading palace guard inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sele rose to first-class ashan i hafan, then to second-class jingkini hafan, and was promoted to leading palace guard inner minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡勤悫。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Qinque.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Qinque.

sentences.zh: 阿賚子吉哈禮，自有傳。

translations.literal: Asai's son Jihali has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Asai's son Jihali has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 慧哲郡王額爾袞，景祖第二子。

translations.literal: Prince of Sagacious Wisdom Ergun was the second son of Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Ergun, Prince of Sagacious Wisdom, was Emperor Jingzu's second son.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，追封諡，配享太廟。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed with a posthumous title and granted joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 he received posthumous enfeoffment and joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 宣獻郡王齋堪，景祖第三子。

translations.literal: Prince of Exalted Offering Zhaikan was the third son of Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaikan, Prince of Exalted Offering, was Emperor Jingzu's third son.

sentences.zh: 當族人與太祖構難，齋堪與額爾袞皆不與。

translations.literal: When kinsmen quarreled with the Taizu, Zhaikan and Ergun took no part.
translations.idiomatic: When clansmen feuded with Taizu, Zhaikan and Ergun stood apart.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，追封諡，配享太廟。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed with a posthumous title and granted joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 he too received posthumous enfeoffment and joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 恪恭貝勒塔察篇古，景祖第五子。

translations.literal: Prince of Reverent Respect Tachapiangu was the fifth son of Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Tachapiangu, Prince of Reverent Respect, was Emperor Jingzu's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 順治間，追封諡。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi reign he was posthumously enfeoffed with a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: During Shunzhi he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: ，詔德世庫等子孫以「覺羅」為氏，系紅帶。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the descendants of Deshiku and others to take "Gioro" as their clan name and wear the red sash.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that the descendants of Deshiku and the rest take "Gioro" as their surname and wear the red sash.

sentences.zh: ，詔國史館：「禮敦等傳列諸臣之首，以別于宗室諸王。」

translations.literal: An edict to the Historiographical Bureau stated: "The biographies of Li Dun and the others are to be placed first among the ministers, to distinguish them from the imperial clansmen who are princes."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict instructed the Historiographical Bureau: "Place the biographies of Li Dun and his line ahead of all other ministers, to distinguish them from princes of the imperial clan."

sentences.zh: 顯祖五子：宣皇后生太祖、莊親王舒爾哈齊、通達郡王雅爾哈齊；

translations.literal: Emperor Xian had five sons: by Empress Xuan, the Taizu, Prince of Zhuang Shu'erhachi, and Prince of Tongda Ya'erhaqi;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu had five sons: by Empress Xuan he fathered Taizu, Prince of Zhuang Shu'erhachi, and Prince of Tongda Ya'erhaqi;

sentences.zh: 繼妃納喇氏生篤義剛果貝勒巴雅喇；

translations.literal: by the consort of the Nara clan, Bayala, Prince of Sincere Righteousness and Bold Achievement;
translations.idiomatic: by the secondary consort of the Nara clan, Bayala, Prince of Sincere Righteousness and Bold Achievement;

sentences.zh: 庶妃李佳氏生誠毅勇壯貝勒莫爾哈齊。

translations.literal: by the concubine of the Li clan, Mo'erhaqi, Prince of Sincere Resolve, Brave Strength, and Martial Valor.
translations.idiomatic: by the concubine of the Li clan, Mo'erhaqi, Prince of Sincere Resolve, Brave Strength, and Martial Valor.

sentences.zh: 誠毅勇壯貝勒莫爾哈齊，顯祖第二子。

translations.literal: Prince of Sincere Resolve, Brave Strength, and Martial Valor Mo'erhaqi was the second son of Emperor Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Mo'erhaqi, Prince of Sincere Resolve, Brave Strength, and Martial Valor, was Emperor Xianzu's second son.

sentences.zh: 驍勇善戰，每先登陷陣。

translations.literal: Fierce and skilled in battle, he was always first to scale walls and break enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and skilled in war, he was always first to scale walls and smash enemy formations.

sentences.zh: 歲乙酉，從太祖伐哲陳部，值大水，遣還，留八十人：被棉甲者五十，被鐵甲者三十，行略地。

translations.literal: In the year yiyou he followed the Taizu against the Zhecheng tribe. Great floods came and he was sent back, leaving eighty men: fifty in cotton armor and thirty in iron armor, to conduct a reconnaissance in force.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiyou year he followed Taizu against the Zhecheng tribe. Heavy floods forced his recall, but eighty men remained—fifty in cotton armor and thirty in iron—to carry out a reconnaissance.

sentences.zh: 加哈人蘇枯賴虎密以告，於是托漠河、章甲、把爾達、撒爾湖、界凡五城合兵禦我。

translations.literal: A man of the Jiaha tribe, Suku laihum, secretly informed them, and the five cities of Tuomohe, Zhangjia, Ba'erda, Sa'erhu, and Jiefan combined their forces to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Suku laihum of the Jiaha people secretly warned them, whereupon the five towns of Tuomohe, Zhangjia, Ba'erda, Sa'erhu, and Jiefan united their troops to oppose the Qing force.

sentences.zh: 後哨章京能古德馳告，上出他道，弗遇。

translations.literal: Rear-guard janggin Nenggude rode in haste to report; the ruler took another route and did not encounter them.
translations.idiomatic: Rear-guard janggin Nenggude galloped back with word; the ruler took another path and avoided contact.

sentences.zh: 上深入，遙望見敵兵八百餘，陣渾河至於南山。

translations.literal: The ruler pressed deep in, and from afar saw more than eight hundred enemy soldiers arrayed from the Hun River to the southern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu pressed deeper in and from a distance saw more than eight hundred enemy soldiers drawn up from the Hun River to the southern hills.

sentences.zh: 包朗阿孫劄親桑古裏懼敵，解其甲授人，上呵之。

translations.literal: Zhaqin Sanguli, grandson of Baolang'a, feared the enemy, removed his armor, and handed it to another; the ruler rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaqin Sanguli, grandson of Baolang'a, feared the foe, stripped off his armor and gave it away; the ruler sharply rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 莫爾哈齊及左右顏布祿、兀浚噶從上馳近敵陣，下馬奮擊，射殺二十餘人，敵渡渾河走。

translations.literal: Mo'erhaqi and his attendants Yanbulu and Wujingga followed the ruler in charging close to the enemy line, dismounted, and fought fiercely, shooting down more than twenty; the enemy crossed the Hun River and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mo'erhaqi with Yanbulu and Wujingga at his side charged with the ruler to the enemy front, dismounted, and fought fiercely, shooting down more than twenty men before the foe fled across the Hun River.

sentences.zh: 莫爾哈齊復從上躡敵後，至吉林崖，遙見敵兵十五自旁徑來。

translations.literal: Mo'erhaqi again followed the ruler in pursuit behind the enemy as far as Jilin Cliff, where from afar fifteen enemy soldiers were seen coming by a side path.
translations.idiomatic: Mo'erhaqi again followed in pursuit to Jilin Cliff, where fifteen enemy soldiers were seen approaching along a side path.

sentences.zh: 上去胄上纓，隱而待，射其前至者，貫脊殪。

translations.literal: The ruler removed his helmet tassel, concealed himself, and waited; he shot the foremost man, piercing his spine and killing him.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler doffed his helmet plume, hid, and waited; he shot the foremost man clean through the spine and killed him.

sentences.zh: 莫爾哈齊復射殪其一，餘皆墜崖死。

translations.literal: Mo'erhaqi again shot and killed one; the rest all fell from the cliff to their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Mo'erhaqi shot another dead; the rest plunged from the cliff and perished.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「今日以四人敗八百人，天助我也！」

translations.literal: The ruler said: "Today four men defeated eight hundred—Heaven has aided us!"
translations.idiomatic: The ruler said, "Today four men routed eight hundred—Heaven has aided us!"

sentences.zh: 莫爾哈齊屢從征伐，賜號青巴圖魯，譯言「誠毅」。

translations.literal: Mo'erhaqi repeatedly followed campaigns and was granted the title Qing Baturu, translated as "sincere resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Mo'erhaqi campaigned repeatedly and was granted the title Qing Baturu, meaning "sincere resolve."

sentences.zh: 天命五年九月，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Tianming he died at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tianming 5 he died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 上臨祭其墓。

translations.literal: The ruler personally attended sacrifice at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler went in person to offer sacrifice at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，追封諡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed with a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子十一，有爵者六：達爾察、務達海、漢岱、塔海、祜世塔、喇世塔。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons; six held noble rank: Da'ercha, Wudahai, Handai, Tahai, Hushita, and Lashita.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons; six held noble titles: Da'ercha, Wudahai, Handai, Tahai, Hushita, and Lashita.

sentences.zh: 達爾察、塔海、祜世塔、喇世塔皆封輔國公，達爾察諡剛毅，喇世塔諡恪僖。

translations.literal: Da'ercha, Tahai, Hushita, and Lashita were all enfeoffed as dukes of the state; Da'ercha received the posthumous title Gangyi and Lashita Gexi.
translations.idiomatic: Da'ercha, Tahai, Hushita, and Lashita were all made dukes of the state; Da'ercha received the posthumous title Gangyi and Lashita Gexi.

sentences.zh: 襄敏貝子務達海，莫爾哈齊第四子。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiang and Keen Sensitivity Wudahai was the fourth son of Mo'erhaqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wudahai, Prince of Xiang and Keen Sensitivity, was Mo'erhaqi's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 事太宗，授牛錄章京。

translations.literal: He served the Taizong and was appointed niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He served Taizong and was appointed niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從睿親王多爾袞伐明，攻沙河、南和及臨洺關、魏縣並有功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed Prince Dorgon in attacking the Ming, assaulting Shahe, Nanhe, and Linming Pass and Weixian, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he followed Prince Dorgon against the Ming, attacking Shahe, Nanhe, Linming Pass, and Weixian, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 三年，授刑部左參政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed left vice-president of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made left vice-president of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 從貝勒嶽讬敗明兵開平，復偕固山額真何洛會等敗明兵沙河、三河，又敗之渾河岸，至趙州。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Yuetuo in defeating Ming troops at Kaiping, and together with gushan ejen Hohor and others defeated Ming troops at Shahe and Sanhe, again defeated them on the banks of the Hun River, and advanced to Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Yuetuo in defeating Ming forces at Kaiping, and with gushan ejen Hohor and others routed Ming troops at Shahe and Sanhe, beat them again on the Hun River, and pushed on to Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 復攻山東，克臨清、安丘、臨淄。

translations.literal: He again attacked Shandong, capturing Linqing, Anqiu, and Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again in Shandong, taking Linqing, Anqiu, and Linzi.

sentences.zh: 還次密雲，俘四千餘。

translations.literal: On the return march he halted at Miyun and took more than four thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he halted at Miyun and took more than four thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 五年，授鑲白旗滿洲梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Manchu meiren ejen of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Manchu meiren ejen of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 從攻錦州，夜略杏山、塔山。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Jinzhou and by night raided Xingshan and Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Jinzhou and by night raided Xingshan and Tashan.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢刑部承政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to president of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to president of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 從伐明，分軍略登州，未至先歸，坐奪俘獲入官。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Ming, detached troops to raid Dengzhou, returned before they arrived, and for this his captives were confiscated for the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Ming campaign and sent a detachment against Dengzhou, but turned back before it arrived; his spoils were seized for the treasury as punishment.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從定京師，逐李自成至延安，城兵夜出，擊破之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed in securing the capital, pursued Li Zicheng to Yan'an, and when garrison troops sallied at night, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he helped secure Beijing, pursued Li Zicheng to Yan'an, and routed a night sortie from the city garrison.

sentences.zh: 復從豫親王多鐸徇江南。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince Dorgon in pacifying the Jiangnan region.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Prince Dorgon in the conquest of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 三年，又從討蘇尼特騰機思，敗土謝圖汗、碩雷汗援兵。

translations.literal: In the third year he again followed the campaign against Tengjisi of the Sunite tribe and defeated the relief forces of Tuxie Khan and Shuolei Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he campaigned again against Tengjisi of the Sunite and defeated the relief armies of Tuxie Khan and Shuolei Khan.

sentences.zh: 五年，偕固山額真阿賴等戍漢中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with gushan ejen Alai and others, he garrisoned Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he garrisoned Hanzhong alongside gushan ejen Alai and others.

sentences.zh: 累進爵，自三等輔國將軍至貝子。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced in rank, from third-class assistant prince of the state to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: His rank rose step by step from third-class assistant prince of the state to beizi.

sentences.zh: 六年，偕鎮國公屯齊哈、輔國公巴布泰代英親王阿濟格討叛將薑瓖。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, together with Prince of the State Tunqiha and Assistant Prince of the State Babutai, he replaced Prince of Ying Ajige in suppressing the rebel general Jiang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he and Princes Tunqiha and Babutai took over from Prince of Ying Ajige to suppress the rebel Jiang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 八年，攝都察院事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he acted as head of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as acting head of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從鄭親王世子濟度討鄭成功，中道疾作，召還。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed the heir of Prince of Zheng Jidu against Zheng Chenggong; illness struck mid-campaign and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined Prince of Zheng's heir Jidu against Zheng Chenggong, but fell ill en route and was recalled.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，諡襄敏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died and was given the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year and received the posthumous title Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 務達海子托克托慧，封鎮國公。

translations.literal: Wudahai's son Toktohui was enfeoffed as Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Wudahai's son Toktohui was enfeoffed as a prince of the state.

sentences.zh: 托克托慧子揚福，事聖祖，官黑龍江將軍久，聖祖屢稱之，命襲不入八分鎮國公。

translations.literal: Toktohui's son Yangfu served the Kangxi Emperor, long held the post of general of Heilongjiang, was repeatedly praised by the emperor, and was ordered to inherit the rank of Prince of the State not admitted to the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Toktohui's son Yangfu served Kangxi as general of Heilongjiang for many years, won repeated praise, and was ordered to inherit the rank of prince of the state outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡襄毅。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 揚福子三官保，聖祖褒其孝，即命繼揚福署黑龍江將軍，襲爵。

translations.literal: Yangfu's son Sanguanbao—the emperor commended his filial piety and immediately ordered him to succeed Yangfu in acting as general of Heilongjiang and to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: Yangfu's son Sanguanbao won Kangxi's praise for filial devotion and was at once ordered to succeed his father as acting general of Heilongjiang and to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 漢岱，莫爾哈齊第五子。

translations.literal: Handai was the fifth son of Mo'erhaqi.
translations.idiomatic: Handai was Mo'erhaqi's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 事太宗，與務達海同授牛錄章京。

translations.literal: Serving the Taizong, he and Wudahai were alike appointed niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he and Wudahai were both appointed niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 崇德六年，從上圍松山，擊破明總兵吳三桂、王樸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongde he followed the ruler in besieging Songshan and defeated the Ming generals Wu Sangui and Wang Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 6 he joined the siege of Songshan and defeated Ming generals Wu Sangui and Wang Pu.

sentences.zh: 七年，從貝勒阿巴泰伐明，攻薊州、河間、景州，進克兗州，即軍前授兵部承政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Prince Abatai against the Ming, attacked Jizhou, Hejian, and Jingzhou, advanced to capture Yanzhou, and was appointed president of the Board of War on the march.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed Prince Abatai against the Ming, took Jizhou, Hejian, and Jingzhou, captured Yanzhou, and was appointed president of the Board of War in the field.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關擊李自成，又從多鐸西征，破自成潼關。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the passes to strike Li Zicheng, and again followed Dorgon westward, defeating Zicheng at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he entered the passes against Li Zicheng and again followed Dorgon west, defeating Zicheng at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 二年，與梅勒額真伊爾德率兵自南陽趨歸德，克州一、縣四；

translations.literal: In the second year, with meiren ejen E'erd, he led troops from Nanyang toward Guide and captured one prefecture and four counties;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he and meiren ejen E'erd marched from Nanyang toward Guide and took one prefecture and four counties;

sentences.zh: 渡淮克揚州。

translations.literal: crossed the Huai and captured Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: then crossed the Huai and captured Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賜金二十五兩、銀千三百兩。

translations.literal: He was granted twenty-five taels of gold and 1,300 taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He received twenty-five taels of gold and 1,300 taels of silver as reward.

sentences.zh: 三年，授鑲白旗滿洲固山額真，與貝勒博洛徇杭州，進攻台州，擊明魯王以海。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Manchu gushan ejen of the Bordered White Banner and with Prince Boluo pacified Hangzhou, advanced to attack Taizhou, and struck the Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Manchu gushan ejen of the Bordered White Banner and with Prince Boluo took Hangzhou, pushed on to Taizhou, and fought the Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai.

sentences.zh: 分兵略福建，攻分水關，破明唐王將師福，入崇安，斬所置巡撫楊文英等，下興化、漳州、泉州。

translations.literal: Troops were divided to overrun Fujian, attacked Fenshui Pass, defeated the Ming Prince of Tang's general Shi Fu, entered Chong'an, beheaded the appointed grand coordinator Yang Wenying and others, and took Xinghua, Zhangzhou, and Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A detachment overran Fujian, stormed Fenshui Pass, defeated the Ming Prince of Tang's general Shi Fu, entered Chong'an, executed Grand Coordinator Yang Wenying and others, and seized Xinghua, Zhangzhou, and Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，從貝子屯齊將兵討陝西亂回。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Prince Tunqi in leading troops to suppress the rebellious Muslims of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Prince Tunqi to suppress Muslim rebels in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 亂定，與英親王阿濟格合軍討叛將薑瓖。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, he united with Prince of Ying Ajige to suppress the rebel general Jiang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he joined Prince of Ying Ajige against the rebel Jiang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 六年，從巽親王滿達海克朔州、甯武。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince of Xun Mandahai in capturing Shuozhou and Ningwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Prince of Xun Mandahai in taking Shuozhou and Ningwu.

sentences.zh: 移師攻遼州，下長留、襄垣、榆社、武鄉諸縣。

translations.literal: Shifting his forces he attacked Liaozhou and took Changliu, Xiangyuan, Yuzhe, and Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned on Liaozhou and captured Changliu, Xiangyuan, Yuzhe, and Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 七年，授吏部尚書、正藍旗滿洲固山額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Minister of Personnel and Manchu gushan ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Minister of Personnel and Manchu gushan ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 八年，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was moved to the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 累進爵，自一等奉國將軍至鎮國公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced in rank, from first-class bannerman of the state to Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: His rank rose from first-class bannerman of the state to prince of the state.

sentences.zh: 九年，復調吏部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again transferred to the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he returned to the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 從定遠大將軍尼堪下湖南，尼堪戰沒，坐奪爵。

translations.literal: He followed the Far Pacification General Nikan south into Hunan; Nikan fell in battle and Handai was stripped of his title for the fault.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Far Pacification General Nikan into Hunan; when Nikan was killed in battle Handai lost his title for shared responsibility.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復授吏部尚書，加太子太保，授鎮國將軍品級。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was again appointed Minister of Personnel, made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted the rank of general of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was reappointed Minister of Personnel, made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted the rank of general of the state.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，坐依阿蒙蔽，奪官爵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, for fawning and concealment he was stripped of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year he lost office and title for currying favor and covering up wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 漢岱子海蘭、席布錫倫、嵩布圖，均封輔國公。

translations.literal: Handai's sons Hailan, Xibuxilun, and Songbutu were all enfeoffed as dukes of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Handai's sons Hailan, Xibuxilun, and Songbutu were all made dukes of the state.

sentences.zh: 海蘭諡悫厚，席布錫倫諡悼敏，嵩布圖諡懷思。

translations.literal: Hailan received the posthumous title Quehou, Xibuxilun Daomin, and Songbutu Huaisi.
translations.idiomatic: Hailan received the posthumous title Quehou, Xibuxilun Daomin, and Songbutu Huaisi.

sentences.zh: 莊親王舒爾哈齊，顯祖第三子。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhuang Shu'erhachi was the third son of Emperor Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Shu'erhachi, Prince of Zhuang, was Emperor Xianzu's third son.

sentences.zh: 初為貝勒。

translations.literal: At first he was a beile.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made a beile.

sentences.zh: 蜚悠城長策穆特黑苦烏喇之虐，原來附。

translations.literal: Cemuhutai, chief of Feiyoucheng, complained of Ula's cruelty and wished to come over.
translations.idiomatic: Cemuhutai, chief of Feiyoucheng, lamented Ula's oppression and sought to submit.

sentences.zh: 太祖令舒爾哈齊及貝勒褚英、代善，諸將費英東、揚古利、常書，侍衛扈爾漢、納齊布，將三千人往迎之。

translations.literal: The Taizu ordered Shu'erhachi and Prince Chuying, Prince Daishan, the generals Fiyanggū, Yangguli, and Changshu, and the guards Hurhan and Naqibu, with three thousand men to go welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Shu'erhachi with Prince Chuying, Prince Daishan, generals Fiyanggū, Yangguli, and Changshu, and guards Hurhan and Naqibu—three thousand men in all—to receive them.

sentences.zh: 夜陰晦，軍行，纛有光，舒爾哈齊曰：「吾從上行兵屢矣，未見此異，其非吉兆耶？」

translations.literal: The night was dark; as the army marched, light shone on the banners. Shu'erhachi said: "I have followed the ruler on campaign many times and never seen such a sign—is it not ill-omened?"
translations.idiomatic: Marching by night they saw light on the banners. Shu'erhachi said, "I have campaigned with the ruler many times and never seen such a portent—can it be auspicious?"

sentences.zh: 欲還兵，褚英、代善不可。

translations.literal: He wished to turn the army back; Chuying and Daishan would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to withdraw, but Chuying and Daishan refused.

sentences.zh: 至蜚悠，盡收環城屯寨五百戶而歸。

translations.literal: Reaching Feiyou, they gathered five hundred households from the stockades around the city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Feiyou they collected five hundred households from the surrounding stockades and returned.

sentences.zh: 烏喇貝勒布占泰發兵萬人邀于路，褚英、代善力戰破之。

translations.literal: Ula beile Bujantai sent ten thousand men to intercept them on the road; Chuying and Daishan fought fiercely and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Ula beile Bujantai sent ten thousand men to ambush them; Chuying and Daishan fought hard and routed them.

sentences.zh: 舒爾哈齊以五百人止山下，常書、納齊布別將百人從焉。

translations.literal: Shu'erhachi halted five hundred men at the foot of the mountain; Changshu and Naqibu separately led one hundred men with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu'erhachi held five hundred men at the mountain foot with Changshu and Naqibu commanding another hundred.

sentences.zh: 褚英、代善既破敵，乃驅兵前進，繞山行，未能多斬獲。

translations.literal: After Chuying and Daishan had broken the enemy they drove forward, circling the mountain, and could not take many heads.
translations.idiomatic: After Chuying and Daishan broke the enemy they pressed around the mountain and took few heads.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜號達爾漢巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was granted the title Dalhan Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he received the title Dalhan Baturu.

sentences.zh: 既，論常書、納齊布止山下不力戰罪，當死。

translations.literal: Thereafter Changshu and Naqibu were judged guilty of halting at the mountain foot and not fighting hard, punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: Then Changshu and Naqibu were judged for holding the foothills without fighting hard—capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 舒爾哈齊曰：「誅二臣與殺我同。」

translations.literal: Shu'erhachi said: "To execute these two ministers is the same as killing me."
translations.idiomatic: Shu'erhachi said, "Executing these two men is the same as killing me."

sentences.zh: 上乃宥之，罰常書金百，奪納齊布所屬。

translations.literal: The ruler then pardoned them, fining Changshu one hundred taels of gold and stripping Naqibu of his dependents.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler spared them, fining Changshu one hundred taels of gold and confiscating Naqibu's followers.

sentences.zh: 自是上不遣舒爾哈齊將兵。

translations.literal: From then on the ruler no longer sent Shu'erhachi to command troops.
translations.idiomatic: After that Taizu never again sent Shu'erhachi to command armies.

sentences.zh: 舒爾哈齊居恆鬱鬱，語其第一子阿爾通阿、第三子扎薩克圖曰：「吾豈以衣食受覊於人哉？」

translations.literal: Shu'erhachi was habitually depressed and said to his eldest son Altong'a and third son Zasaktu: "Am I to be bound by food and clothing and live at another's pleasure?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu'erhachi grew despondent and told his eldest son Altong'a and third son Zasaktu, "Must I be tethered by food and clothing and live at another's whim?"

sentences.zh: 移居黑扯木。

translations.literal: He moved to reside at Heichemu.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his residence to Heichemu.

sentences.zh: 上怒，誅其二子舒爾哈齊乃復還。

translations.literal: The ruler in anger executed his two sons; only then did Shu'erhachi return.
translations.idiomatic: In anger the ruler executed two of his sons; only then did Shu'erhachi come back.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥八月，薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the year xinhai he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the xinhai year.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，追封諡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed with a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子九，有爵者五：阿敏、圖倫、寨桑武、濟爾哈朗、費揚武。

translations.literal: He had nine sons; five held noble rank: Amin, Tulun, Zaisangwu, Jirhalang, and Feiyangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons; five held noble titles: Amin, Tulun, Zaisangwu, Jirhalang, and Feiyangwu.

sentences.zh: 阿敏，舒爾哈齊第二子。

translations.literal: Amin was the second son of Shu'erhachi.
translations.idiomatic: Amin was Shu'erhachi's second son.

sentences.zh: 歲戊申，偕褚英伐烏喇，克宜罕山城，俘其衆以歸。

translations.literal: In the year wushen, together with Chuying he attacked Ula and captured Yihan Mountain City, bringing back the captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the wushen year he and Chuying attacked Ula, took Yihan Mountain City, and returned with prisoners.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，上伐烏喇，布占泰以三萬人拒，諸將欲戰，上止之。

translations.literal: In the year guichou the ruler attacked Ula; Bujantai resisted with thirty thousand men. The generals wished to fight; the ruler held them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year Taizu attacked Ula; Bujantai met him with thirty thousand men. The generals wanted battle; Taizu restrained them.

sentences.zh: 阿敏曰：「布占泰已出，舍而不戰，將奈何？」

translations.literal: Amin said: "Bujantai has already come out—if we let him go without fighting, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Amin said, "Bujantai is already out—if we refuse battle now, what then?"

sentences.zh: 上乃決戰，遂破烏喇。

translations.literal: The ruler then decided on battle and broke Ula.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then gave battle and destroyed Ula.

sentences.zh: 天命元年，與代善、莽古爾泰及太宗並授和碩貝勒，號「四大貝勒」，執國政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianming, with Daishan, Manggu'ertai, and the Taizong he was alike granted the rank of prince of the state and titled the "Four Great Princes," sharing in government.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 1 he, Daishan, Manggu'ertai, and the future Taizong were all made princes of the state—the "Four Great Princes"—and shared government.

sentences.zh: 阿敏以序稱二貝勒。

translations.literal: Amin by seniority was styled Second Prince.
translations.idiomatic: By seniority Amin was styled Second Prince.

sentences.zh: 四年，明經略楊鎬大舉來侵，阿敏從上擊破明兵薩爾滸山。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Grand Secretary Yang Hao of the Ming came in force; Amin followed the ruler in defeating Ming troops at Mount Sarhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Ming Grand Secretary Yang Hao invaded in strength; Amin followed Taizu in defeating Ming forces at Mount Sarhu.

sentences.zh: 復禦明總兵劉綎于棟鄂路，代善等繼之，陣斬綎。

translations.literal: He again met Ming Commander Liu Ting on the Dong'e Road; Daishan and others followed up and Liu Ting was slain in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He met Ming commander Liu Ting on the Dong'e road; Daishan and others pressed the attack and Liu Ting was killed in the field.

sentences.zh: 還擊明將喬一琦，一琦奔固拉庫崖，與朝鮮將薑弘烈合軍。

translations.literal: Turning back he struck Ming General Qiao Yiqi; Yiqi fled to Gulakuyai Cliff and joined Korean General Jiang Honglie.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back he struck Ming general Qiao Yiqi, who fled to Gulakuyai Cliff and joined the Korean general Jiang Honglie.

sentences.zh: 阿敏攻之，弘烈降。

translations.literal: Amin attacked them and Honglie surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Amin attacked them and Honglie submitted.

sentences.zh: 一琦自經死。

translations.literal: Yiqi hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqi hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 尋從上破葉赫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed the ruler in breaking Yehe.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he followed Taizu in the destruction of Yehe.

sentences.zh: 六人，從上取瀋陽、遼陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the ruler in taking Shenyang and Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Taizu in capturing Shenyang and Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 鎮江城將陳良策叛附明將毛文龍，阿敏遷其民於內地。

translations.literal: Chen Liangce, garrison commander of Zhenjiang City, rebelled and went over to Ming General Mao Wenlong; Amin moved the inhabitants inland.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang garrison commander Chen Liangce defected to Ming general Mao Wenlong; Amin relocated the populace inland.

sentences.zh: 文龍屯兵朝鮮境，阿敏夜渡鎮江，擊殺其守將，文龍敗走。

translations.literal: Wenlong stationed troops on the Korean border; Amin crossed Zhenjiang by night, killed the garrison commander, and Wenlong fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong encamped on the Korean frontier; Amin crossed Zhenjiang by night, killed the garrison commander, and Wenlong fled.

sentences.zh: 十一年，伐喀爾喀巴林部，取所屬屯寨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he attacked the Barin tribe of Khalkha and took their dependent stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he raided the Barin tribe of Khalkha and seized their dependent stockades.

sentences.zh: 伐紮嚕特部，俘其衆。

translations.literal: He attacked the Jarut tribe and took their people captive.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the Jarut tribe and took captives.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，太宗命偕貝勒嶽讬等伐朝鮮，瀕行，上命並討文龍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong the Taizong ordered him with Prince Yuetuo and others to attack Korea; on the eve of departure the ruler also ordered them to strike Wenlong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 Taizong sent him with Prince Yuetuo and others against Korea and ordered them also to destroy Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 師拔義州，分兵攻鐵山，文龍所屯地也，文龍敗走。

translations.literal: The army took Uiju; troops were divided to attack Tieshan, where Wenlong was encamped, and Wenlong fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The army took Uiju and detached forces against Tieshan, Wenlong's base; Wenlong fled.

sentences.zh: 進克定州，渡嘉山江，克安州、平壤。

translations.literal: Advancing they took Dingzhou, crossed the Jiashan River, and captured Anzhou and Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to Dingzhou, crossed the Jiashan River, and took Anzhou and Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 復進次中和，朝鮮國王李倧使迎師。

translations.literal: Pressing on they halted at Zhonghe; King Li Jong of Korea sent envoys to welcome the army.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Zhonghe; King Li Jong sent envoys to welcome the army.

sentences.zh: 阿敏與諸貝勒答書數其罪有七，力拒之。

translations.literal: Amin and the princes replied in a letter listing seven crimes and firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Amin and the princes answered with a letter listing seven crimes and firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 師復進次黃州，倧復遣使來。

translations.literal: The army advanced again to Huangzhou and Jong again sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced to Huangzhou and Jong sent envoys again.

sentences.zh: 阿敏欲遂破其都城，諸貝勒謂宜待其大臣至，蒞盟許平。

translations.literal: Amin wished to break their capital at once; the princes said they should wait until their ministers arrived to swear the covenant and grant peace.
translations.idiomatic: Amin wanted to storm the capital immediately; the other princes urged waiting for Korean ministers to come swear peace.

sentences.zh: 總兵李永芳進曰：「我等奉上命仗義而行，前已遺書言遣大臣蒞盟即班師，背之不義。」

translations.literal: Commander Li Yongfang advanced and said: "We act on the ruler's command in the name of righteousness; we have already written that if ministers come to swear the covenant we will withdraw— to go back on this is unrighteous."
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Yongfang said, "We march under the ruler's righteous mandate and have promised withdrawal once ministers swear the covenant—to break that promise is unrighteous."

sentences.zh: 阿敏怒，叱之退，師復進次平山，倧走江華島，遣其臣進昌君至軍，阿敏令吹角督進兵。

translations.literal: Amin in anger rebuked him to withdraw; the army advanced again to Pingshan. Jong fled to Jianghua Island and sent his minister the Lord of Jinchang to the army; Amin ordered horns blown to press the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Amin angrily dismissed him and marched to Pingshan. Jong fled to Jianghua Island and sent the Lord of Jinchang; Amin ordered trumpets sounded to urge the advance.

sentences.zh: 岳讬乃與濟爾哈朗駐平山，遣副將劉興祚入江華島責倧。

translations.literal: Yuetuo then with Jirhalang halted at Pingshan and sent Vice Commander Liu Xingzuo into Jianghua Island to reproach Jong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuetuo and Jirhalang halted at Pingshan and sent Vice Commander Liu Xingzuo to Jianghua Island to rebuke Jong.

sentences.zh: 倧遣族弟原昌君覺等詣軍，為設宴。

translations.literal: Jong sent his clansman the Lord of Yuanchang Jue and others to the army and a banquet was set.
translations.idiomatic: Jong sent his kinsman the Lord of Yuanchang Jue and others; a banquet was held.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，嶽讬議還師，阿敏曰：「吾恆慕明帝及朝鮮王城郭宮殿，今既至此，何遽歸耶？

translations.literal: When the banquet ended Yuetuo proposed returning; Amin said: "I have long admired the Ming emperor's and the Korean king's walled cities and palaces—now that we are here, why hurry home?
translations.idiomatic: After the feast Yuetuo urged withdrawal; Amin said, "I have long envied the Ming emperor's and the Korean king's walled palaces—now that we are here, why hurry away?

sentences.zh: 我意當留兵屯耕，杜度與我叔侄同居于此。」

translations.literal: My wish is to leave troops to farm and garrison; Dudu and I, uncle and nephew, will dwell here together."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to leave troops to farm and settle; Dudu and I, uncle and nephew, will live here together."

sentences.zh: 杜度變色曰：「上乃我叔，我何肯遠離，何為與爾同居？」

translations.literal: Dudu flushed and said: "The ruler is my uncle—how could I live far from him? Why should I dwell with you?"
translations.idiomatic: Dudu flushed and said, "The ruler is my uncle—why should I live apart from him? Why dwell with you?"

sentences.zh: 濟爾哈朗亦力阻，諸貝勒乃定議許倧盟。

translations.literal: Jirhalang also strongly opposed; the princes then fixed on allowing Jong to swear the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang also objected firmly; the princes then agreed to let Jong swear peace.

sentences.zh: 阿敏縱兵掠三日，乃還。

translations.literal: Amin let his troops plunder for three days and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Amin allowed three days of plunder and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上迎勞于武靖營，賜禦衣一襲。

translations.literal: The ruler welcomed and rewarded them at Wujing Camp and granted one suit of imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu welcomed them at Wujing Camp, rewarded them, and granted a suit of imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 復從上伐明，圍錦州，攻寧遠，斬明步卒千餘。

translations.literal: He again followed the ruler against the Ming, besieged Jinzhou, attacked Ningyuan, and beheaded more than a thousand Ming foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Taizu against the Ming, besieged Jinzhou, attacked Ningyuan, and slew more than a thousand Ming foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 四年，師克永平、灤州、遷安、遵化，上命阿敏偕貝勒碩讬將五千人駐守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the army took Yongping, Luanchuan, Qian'an, and Zunhua; the ruler ordered Amin with Prince Shuotuo to garrison with five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the army took Yongping, Luanchuan, Qian'an, and Zunhua; Taizu ordered Amin and Prince Shuotuo to garrison with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 阿敏駐永平，分遣諸將分守三城，諭降榛子鎮。

translations.literal: Amin garrisoned Yongping and detached generals to hold the other three cities, inducing Zhenzi Town to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Amin held Yongping, posted generals to the other three cities, and induced Zhenzi Town to surrender.

sentences.zh: 明經略孫承宗督兵攻灤州，阿敏遣數百人赴援，收遷安守兵入永平。

translations.literal: Ming Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong led troops against Luanchuan; Amin sent several hundred men to relieve it and gathered the Qian'an garrison into Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong attacked Luanchuan; Amin sent several hundred reinforcements and pulled the Qian'an garrison into Yongping.

sentences.zh: 明兵攻灤州急，灤州守將固山額真圖爾格等不能支，棄城奔永平，明兵截擊，師死者四百餘。

translations.literal: Ming forces pressed Luanchuan hard; gushan ejen Turg and other defenders could not hold out, abandoned the city, and fled to Yongping; Ming troops intercepted them and more than four hundred soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Ming pressure on Luanchuan grew unbearable; gushan ejen Turg and the garrison fled to Yongping; Ming troops cut them down and more than four hundred soldiers perished.

sentences.zh: 阿敏令遵化守將固山額真察哈喇等亦棄其城，遂盡殺明將吏降者，屠城民，收其金帛，夜出冷口東還。

translations.literal: Amin ordered Zunhua's garrison gushan ejen Chahala and others also to abandon their city; he then killed all Ming officers and soldiers who had surrendered, slaughtered the townspeople, gathered gold and silks, and by night marched out through Lengkou to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Amin ordered Zunhua's gushan ejen Chahala and others to abandon their city as well; he then slaughtered surrendered Ming officers and soldiers, massacred the townspeople, seized gold and silk, and fled east by night through Lengkou.

sentences.zh: 上方遣貝勒杜度赴援，聞阿敏等棄四城而歸，上御殿，集諸貝勒大臣宣諭，罪阿敏等。

translations.literal: The ruler above sent Prince Dudu to relieve them; hearing that Amin and others had abandoned the four cities and returned, the ruler ascended the hall, gathered the princes and ministers, proclaimed an edict, and charged Amin and others with crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Prince Dudu to relieve the garrisons; when he learned that Amin and the others had abandoned the four cities and withdrawn, he took the throne, assembled princes and ministers, proclaimed their guilt, and arraigned Amin and his associates.

sentences.zh: 阿敏等至，令屯距城十五里，復宣諭詰責。

translations.literal: When Amin and the others arrived he ordered them encamped fifteen li from the city and again proclaimed edicts of reproach.
translations.idiomatic: When Amin's party arrived he made them camp fifteen li from the city and again publicly rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 上念士卒陷敵，感傷墮淚。

translations.literal: The ruler, thinking of soldiers trapped among the enemy, was moved to grief and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning soldiers lost to the enemy, the ruler wept.

sentences.zh: 越三日，召諸貝勒大臣集闕下，上御殿，令貝勒岳讬宣於衆曰：「阿敏怙惡久矣。

translations.literal: Three days later he summoned the princes and ministers below the palace gate; ascending the hall he ordered Prince Yuetuo to proclaim to the assembly: "Amin has long been willfully wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he gathered princes and ministers at the palace gate and had Prince Yuetuo announce to all: "Amin's wickedness goes back many years.

sentences.zh: 當太祖時，嗾其父欲移居黑扯木，太祖坐其父子罪，既而宥之。

translations.literal: In the time of the Taizu he incited his father to move to Heichemu; the Taizu punished father and son, then pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu he urged his father to relocate to Heichemu; Taizu punished father and son, then pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 其父既終，太祖愛養阿敏如己出，授為和碩貝勒。

translations.literal: After his father died the Taizu cherished and raised Amin as his own son and granted him the rank of prince of the state.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death Taizu reared Amin like his own son and made him a prince of the state.

sentences.zh: 及上嗣位，禮待如初。

translations.literal: When the ruler succeeded to the throne he treated him with the same courtesy as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne he treated Amin with the same honor as before.

sentences.zh: 師征朝鮮，既定盟受質，不原班師，欲與杜度居王京，濟爾哈朗力諫乃止。

translations.literal: On the Korean campaign, after the covenant was settled and hostages taken, he would not agree to withdraw but wished to dwell with Dudu in the king's capital; only Jirhalang's strong remonstrance stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: On the Korean campaign, after peace and hostages, he refused to withdraw and wanted to settle with Dudu in the royal capital; only Jirhalang's firm opposition stopped him.

sentences.zh: 此阿敏有異志之見端也。

translations.literal: This was the first sign of Amin's rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: This was the first clear sign of Amin's disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 俘美婦進上，既，復自求之。

translations.literal: He presented a beautiful woman to the ruler; afterward he asked for her back.
translations.idiomatic: He offered a beautiful captive to the ruler, then demanded her back.

sentences.zh: 上察其觖望，曰：『奈何以一婦人乖兄弟之好？』

translations.literal: The ruler perceived his discontent and said: "How can we let one woman harm brotherly affection?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his resentment, the ruler said, "How can one woman come between brothers?"

sentences.zh: 以賜總兵冷格裏。

translations.literal: He gave her to Commander Lenggeli.
translations.idiomatic: He gave her to Commander Lenggeli.

sentences.zh: 伐察哈爾，土謝圖額駙背約與通好，上怒，絕之。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Chakhar, Tuxie the son-in-law broke the covenant and made friendly contact; the ruler in anger broke relations.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Chakhar, son-in-law Tuxie broke treaty and made overtures; the ruler angrily cut ties.

sentences.zh: 阿敏遺以甲胄鞍轡，且以上語盡告之。

translations.literal: Amin sent him armor, saddles, and bridles, and told him everything the ruler had said.
translations.idiomatic: Amin sent him armor and horse gear and repeated to him everything the ruler had said.

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒子女婚嫁必聞上，阿敏私以女嫁蒙古貝勒塞特爾，及宴，上不往，常懷怨憤。

translations.literal: When princes' sons and daughters married they had to inform the ruler; Amin privately married his daughter to Mongol beile Setter and at the feast the ruler did not attend—he constantly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Princes had to report children's marriages to the throne; Amin privately married his daughter to Mongol beile Setter, and when the ruler skipped the feast he nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，守邊駐防，原有定界，乃越界移駐黑扯木。

translations.literal: In the Taizu era frontier garrisons had fixed boundaries; he crossed the border and moved his post to Heichemu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu frontier posts had fixed boundaries; he crossed them and moved his garrison to Heichemu.

sentences.zh: 上責以擅棄汛地，將有異志，阿敏不能答。

translations.literal: The ruler charged him with abandoning the defense line at will and harboring rebellious intent; Amin could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler accused him of willfully abandoning the defense line and disloyal designs; Amin had no reply.

sentences.zh: 上出征，令阿敏留守，惟耽逸樂，屢出行獵。

translations.literal: When the ruler campaigned he left Amin to guard the capital; Amin only indulged in pleasure and went hunting again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler marched out he left Amin in charge; Amin idled in pleasure and hunted repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 嶽讬、豪格出師先還，坐受其拜，儼如國君。

translations.literal: When Yuetuo and Hooge returned from campaign ahead of schedule he accepted their bows as if he were the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuetuo and Hooge returned early from campaign he accepted their bows as though he were sovereign.

sentences.zh: 及代守永平，妄曰：『既克城，何故不殺其民？』

translations.literal: While acting garrison commander at Yongping he rashly said: "Since we have taken the city, why not kill its people?"
translations.idiomatic: As Yongping garrison commander he said rashly, "We have taken the city—why spare its people?"

sentences.zh: 又明告衆兵曰：『我既來此，豈能令爾等不飽欲而歸？』

translations.literal: He also openly told the troops: "Now that I am here, how can I let you return without your fill of loot?"
translations.idiomatic: He told the soldiers openly, "Now that I am here, how can I send you home empty-handed?"

sentences.zh: 略榛子鎮，盡掠其財物，又驅降人分給八家為奴。

translations.literal: He raided Zhenzi Town and plundered all its goods, then drove the surrendered people to be divided as slaves among the Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: He plundered Zhenzi Town, seized its wealth, and distributed surrendered people as slaves among the Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 明兵圍灤州三晝夜，擁兵不親援，屠永平、遷安官民，悉載財帛牲畜以歸。

translations.literal: Ming troops besieged Luanchuan for three days and nights; he held his army back and did not relieve it in person, slaughtered the officials and people of Yongping and Qian'an, and loaded wealth, cloth, and livestock to return.
translations.idiomatic: Ming forces besieged Luanchuan for three days and nights while he held back from personal relief, massacred Yongping and Qian'an, and returned laden with goods and livestock.

sentences.zh: 毀壞基業，故令我軍傷殘。」

translations.literal: He destroyed the foundation of our achievement and therefore caused our army casualties."
translations.idiomatic: He wrecked what we had built and brought casualties on our army."

sentences.zh: 命議其罪。

translations.literal: He ordered deliberation on his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his crimes debated.

sentences.zh: 僉曰：「當誅。」

translations.literal: All said: "He should be executed."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "He deserves death."

sentences.zh: 命幽之。

translations.literal: He ordered him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 留莊六所、園二所、奴僕二十、羊五百、牛二十，餘財產悉畀濟爾哈朗。

translations.literal: He left him six estates, two gardens, twenty slaves, five hundred sheep, and twenty cattle; the rest of his property was all given to Jirhalang.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed six estates, two gardens, twenty slaves, five hundred sheep, and twenty cattle; the rest went to Jirhalang.

sentences.zh: 崇德五年十一月，卒於幽所。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year of Chongde he died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Chongde 5 he died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 阿敏子六，有爵者五：愛爾禮、固爾瑪琿、恭阿、果盖、果賴。

translations.literal: Amin had six sons; five held noble rank: Aierli, Gu'ermahui, Gong'a, Guogai, and Guolai.
translations.idiomatic: Amin had six sons; five held titles: Aierli, Gu'ermahui, Gong'a, Guogai, and Guolai.

sentences.zh: 愛爾禮、果盖、果賴皆封鎮國公，愛爾禮坐罪死，果盖諡端純。

translations.literal: Aierli, Guogai, and Guolai were all enfeoffed as princes of the state; Aierli died for a crime, and Guogai received the posthumous title Duanchun.
translations.idiomatic: Aierli, Guogai, and Guolai became princes of the state; Aierli was executed for crime, and Guogai received the posthumous title Duanchun.

sentences.zh: 溫簡貝子固爾瑪琿，崇德間，從多爾袞伐明，自京師入山西境，復東至濟南，克城四十餘，封輔國公。

translations.literal: Prince of Warm Simplicity Gu'ermahui, in the Chongde era, followed Dorgon against the Ming, entered Shanxi from the capital region, turned east to Jinan, and captured more than forty cities; he was enfeoffed as duke of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Gu'ermahui, Prince of Warm Simplicity, followed Dorgon against the Ming in Chongde, entered Shanxi from Beijing, turned east to Jinan, and took more than forty cities, earning the rank of duke of the state.

sentences.zh: 阿敏得罪，奪爵，削宗籍。

translations.literal: When Amin was condemned his title was stripped and he was removed from the imperial clan register.
translations.idiomatic: When Amin fell, his title was stripped and he was struck from the clan register.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，復封輔國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he was again enfeoffed as duke of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 he was re-enfeoffed as duke of the state.

sentences.zh: 上以其貧乏，賜白金三千。

translations.literal: Because he was poor the ruler granted him three thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Finding him impoverished, the court granted three thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 從濟爾哈朗徇湖廣，破何騰蛟。

translations.literal: He followed Jirhalang in pacifying Huguang and defeated He Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Jirhalang in pacifying Huguang and defeated He Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 師復進攻永興，奪門入，敗明兵，進貝子。

translations.literal: The army advanced again to attack Yongxing, stormed the gate, defeated Ming troops, and he was advanced to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Yongxing he stormed the gates, routed Ming forces, and was raised to beizi.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十年，卒，諡溫簡。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kangxi he died and was given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 20 and received the posthumous title Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 鎮國襄敏公瓦三，固爾瑪琿子。

translations.literal: Prince of the State Xiangmin Wasan was the son of Gu'ermahui.
translations.idiomatic: Wasan, Prince of the State Xiangmin, was Gu'ermahui's son.

sentences.zh: 事聖祖，初封輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Serving the Kangxi Emperor, he was first enfeoffed as assistant prince of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he was first made assistant prince of the state.

sentences.zh: 從嶽讬定湖廣，襲輔國公。

translations.literal: He followed Yuetuo in pacifying Huguang and inherited the rank of duke of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuetuo in pacifying Huguang and inherited the ducal title.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，授右宗人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed right director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he became right director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 追論攻長沙退縮罪，奪官，仍留爵。

translations.literal: Reckoning afterward the fault of shrinking back at the attack on Changsha, he was stripped of office but kept his title.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was judged for hesitating at Changsha, lost office, but kept his title.

sentences.zh: 復授鑲藍旗滿州固山額真。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Manchu gushan ejen of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Manchu gushan ejen of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 俄羅斯侵據雅克薩，上遣瓦三偕侍郎果丕，會黑龍江將軍薩布素按治。

translations.literal: Russia invaded and occupied Albazin; the emperor sent Wasan with Vice President Guobi and Heilongjiang General Sabusu to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Russia seized Albazin, Kangxi sent Wasan with Vice President Guobi and General Sabusu of Heilongjiang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 尋命固山額真朋春等率師討之，以瓦三統轄黑龍江將士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward gushan ejen Pengchun and others were ordered to lead troops against them; Wasan commanded the Heilongjiang forces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon gushan ejen Pengchun and others were sent to attack; Wasan commanded Heilongjiang troops.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒，諡襄敏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died and was given the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fourth year and received the posthumous title Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 瓦三子齊克塔哈，襲輔國公。

translations.literal: Wasan's son Qiketaha inherited the rank of duke of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wasan's son Qiketaha inherited the ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 事聖祖，征噶爾丹在行。

translations.literal: Serving the Kangxi Emperor, he campaigned against Galdan on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he campaigned against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 曆右宗人、都統、領侍衛大臣。

translations.literal: He served as right director of the Imperial Clan Court, commandant-in-chief, and leading palace guard minister.
translations.idiomatic: He held posts as right clan director, commandant-in-chief, and leading palace guard minister.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: For an offense he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he lost his title.

sentences.zh: 以固爾瑪琿孫鄂斐襲。

translations.literal: Gu'ermahui's grandson Efei inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Gu'ermahui's grandson Efei inherited.

sentences.zh: 征噶爾丹亦在行。

translations.literal: He also campaigned against Galdan on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He too campaigned against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 卒，以子鄂齊襲。

translations.literal: He died and his son Eqi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died and his son Eqi inherited.

sentences.zh: 事世宗，嘗奉使西藏，宣諭達賴喇嘛，進鎮國公。

translations.literal: Serving the Yongzheng Emperor, he once went as envoy to Tibet to proclaim edicts to the Dalai Lama and was advanced to Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he served as envoy to Tibet to address the Dalai Lama and was raised to prince of the state.

sentences.zh: 授天津水師都統，坐不能約束所部，奪爵。

translations.literal: Appointed commandant of the Tianjin naval forces, for failing to restrain his troops he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: As commandant of the Tianjin navy he lost his title for failing to control his men.

sentences.zh: 復起授都統，坐納賂，再奪爵。

translations.literal: Reappointed commandant-in-chief, for accepting bribes he was again stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: Reappointed commandant-in-chief, he lost his title again for taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 恭阿，亦以阿敏得罪，與固爾瑪琿同譴，尋同還宗籍。

translations.literal: Gong'a, also condemned with Amin, was punished together with Gu'ermahui and soon restored to the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Gong'a, implicated with Amin, was punished with Gu'ermahui and soon restored to the clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，同徇湖廣，克六十餘城，封鎮國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he likewise pacified Huguang and captured more than sixty cities; he was enfeoffed as Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 he too pacified Huguang, took more than sixty cities, and was made prince of the state.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the field in the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 鄭獻親王濟爾哈朗，舒爾哈齊第六子。

translations.literal: Prince of Exalted Offering Jirhalang was the sixth son of Shu'erhachi.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang, Prince of Exalted Offering, was Shu'erhachi's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 幼育于太祖。

translations.literal: He was reared in youth by the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu raised him from childhood.

sentences.zh: 封和碩貝勒。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as prince of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a prince of the state.

sentences.zh: 天命十一年，伐喀爾喀巴林部、紮嚕特部，並有功。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianming he attacked the Barin and Jarut tribes of Khalkha, distinguishing himself in both.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 11 he campaigned against Khalkha's Barin and Jarut tribes with distinction.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，伐朝鮮，朝鮮國王李倧既乞盟，阿敏仍欲攻其國都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong, attacking Korea, after King Li Jong had begged for a covenant Amin still wished to assault the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1, on the Korean campaign, after King Li Jong sued for peace Amin still wanted to storm the capital.

sentences.zh: 岳讬邀濟爾哈朗議，濟爾哈朗曰：「吾等不宜深入，當駐兵平山以待。」

translations.literal: Yuetuo invited Jirhalang to counsel; Jirhalang said: "We should not press deep but halt at Pingshan and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Yuetuo consulted Jirhalang, who said, "We should not advance deep but hold at Pingshan and wait."

sentences.zh: 卒定盟而還。

translations.literal: In the end they fixed the covenant and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They finally made peace and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月，從上伐明，圍錦州，偕莽古爾泰擊敗明兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he followed the ruler against the Ming, besieged Jinzhou, and with Manggu'ertai defeated Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he followed the ruler against the Ming, besieged Jinzhou, and with Manggu'ertai routed Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 復移師寧遠，與明總兵滿桂遇，裹創力戰，大敗其衆。

translations.literal: Shifting to Ningyuan they met Ming Commander Man Gui; though wounded he fought fiercely and routed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningyuan they met Ming commander Man Gui; though wounded, Jirhalang fought hard and crushed the foe.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，偕豪格討蒙古固特塔布囊，戮之，收其衆歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, with Hooge he suppressed the Mongol guwang Gututabun, executed him, and brought his people back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year he and Hooge destroyed Mongol leader Gututabun and brought his people in.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，伐明錦州、寧遠，焚其積聚。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year he attacked Ming Jinzhou and Ningyuan and burned their stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year he raided Jinzhou and Ningyuan and burned their granaries.

sentences.zh: 十月，上率師自洪山口入，濟爾哈朗偕嶽讬攻大安口，夜毀水門以進，擊明馬蘭營援兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the ruler led the army in through Hongshan Pass; Jirhalang with Yuetuo attacked Daankou, destroyed the sluice gate by night to advance, and struck Ming relief for Malanying.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the ruler entered through Hongshan Pass; Jirhalang and Yuetuo took Daankou, broke the water gate by night, and hit Ming relief for Malanying.
