sentences.zh: 及旦，明兵立二營山上，濟爾哈朗督兵追擊，五戰皆捷，降馬蘭營、馬蘭口、大安口三營。

translations.literal: At dawn Ming troops stood in two camps on the hills; Jirhalang directed pursuit and won five battles, accepting the surrender of Malanying, Malankou, and Daankou.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Ming forces held two hill camps; Jirhalang pursued, won five fights, and received the surrender of Malanying, Malankou, and Daankou.

sentences.zh: 引軍趨石門寨，殲明援兵，寨民出降。

translations.literal: He led the army toward Shimen Stockade, annihilated Ming relief, and the stockade people came out to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Shimen Stockade, destroyed Ming relief, and the garrison submitted.

sentences.zh: 會師遵化，薄明都，徇通州張家灣。

translations.literal: Joining the main army at Zunhua they pressed the Ming capital and overran Tongzhou and Zhangjiawan.
translations.idiomatic: Rejoining the main force at Zunhua they pressed Beijing and overran Tongzhou and Zhangjiawan.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，從上圍永平，擊斬叛將劉興祚，獲其弟興賢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he followed the ruler in besieging Yongping, struck down the rebel Liu Xingzuo, and captured his brother Xingxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he besieged Yongping, killed rebel Liu Xingzuo, and captured his brother Xingxian.

sentences.zh: 既克永平，與貝勒薩哈璘駐守，察倉庫，閱士卒，置官吏，傳檄下灤州、遷安。

translations.literal: After Yongping fell he with Prince Sahalian garrisoned it, inspected storehouses, reviewed troops, appointed officials, and issued proclamations to bring down Luanchuan and Qian'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongping fell he and Prince Sahalian garrisoned it, inspected stores and troops, appointed officials, and issued summons to Luanchuan and Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 三月，阿敏代戍，乃引師還。

translations.literal: In the third month Amin replaced the garrison and he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Amin relieved him and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，初設六部，濟爾哈朗掌刑部事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year the Six Ministries were first established; Jirhalang headed the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year the Six Ministries were founded; Jirhalang headed Punishments.

sentences.zh: 從上圍大淩河，濟爾哈朗督兵收近城台堡。

translations.literal: He followed the ruler in besieging Dalinghe; Jirhalang directed troops in taking nearby walled towers and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Dalinghe he took nearby towers and stockades.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，從征察哈爾，還趨歸化城，收其衆千餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year he campaigned against Chakhar and on the return hurried to Guide City, gathering more than a thousand of their people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year he campaigned against Chakhar and on the return swept Guide City, gathering more than a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，城岫岩。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year he walled Xiuyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he fortified Xiuyan.

sentences.zh: 五月，明將孔有德、耿仲明自登州來降，明總兵黃龍以水師邀之，朝鮮兵與會，濟爾哈朗與貝勒阿濟格等勒軍自鎮江迓有德等，明兵引去。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ming generals Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming defected from Dengzhou; Ming Commander Huang Long with a fleet and Korean troops intercepted them; Jirhalang with Prince Ajige and others led troops from Zhenjiang to meet Youde and the others, and Ming forces withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming defected from Dengzhou; Huang Long and Korean allies tried to block them; Jirhalang and Prince Ajige met the defectors at Zhenjiang and Ming ships withdrew.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年四月，封和碩鄭親王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Chongde he was enfeoffed as Prince of Exalted Offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Chongde 1 he was made Prince of Exalted Offering.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，攻甯遠，薄中後所城，明兵不敢出。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year he attacked Ningyuan and pressed Zhonghou Fort; Ming troops dared not sally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year he attacked Ningyuan and pressed Zhonghou Fort while Ming troops stayed inside.

sentences.zh: 移師克模龍關及五里堡屯台。

translations.literal: Shifting his forces he took Molong Pass and the Wulibao tower stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Molong Pass and the Wulibao tower stockade.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，略錦州、松山，九戰皆勝，俘其衆二千有奇。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he raided Jinzhou and Songshan, winning nine battles and taking more than two thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he raided Jinzhou and Songshan, won nine fights, and took more than two thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，修義州城。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year he repaired Yizhou city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year he repaired Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 蒙古多羅特部蘇班岱、阿爾巴岱附於明，屯杏山五里台，請以三十戶來歸。

translations.literal: Subanai and Arbatai of the Dorot tribe of Mongolia, attached to the Ming and encamped at Xingshan Wulitai, asked to come over with thirty households.
translations.idiomatic: Subanai and Arbatai of Mongolia's Dorot tribe, Ming allies at Xingshan Wulitai, offered to defect with thirty households.

sentences.zh: 上命率師千五百人迎之，戒曰：「明兵見我寡，必來戰，可分軍為三隊以行。」

translations.literal: The ruler ordered him to lead fifteen hundred men to welcome them, warning: "If Ming troops see us few they will surely fight; divide the army in three columns on the march."
translations.idiomatic: The ruler sent him with fifteen hundred men to receive them, warning that Ming forces would attack if they saw a small column and ordering the march in three divisions."

sentences.zh: 夜過錦州，至杏山，使潛告蘇班岱等攜輜重以行。

translations.literal: By night they passed Jinzhou and reached Xingshan, secretly telling Subanai and the others to move with their baggage.
translations.idiomatic: By night they passed Jinzhou and reached Xingshan, secretly instructing Subanai's group to move with their baggage.

sentences.zh: 旦，明杏山總兵劉周智與錦州、松山守將合兵七千逼我師，濟爾哈朗縱師入敵陣，大敗之，賜禦厩良馬一。

translations.literal: At dawn Ming Xingshan Commander Liu Zhouzhi with Jinzhou and Songshan garrison commanders united seven thousand men and pressed the Qing force; Jirhalang charged into the enemy line and routed them, and was granted one fine horse from the imperial stables.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Liu Zhouzhi of Xingshan with Jinzhou and Songshan commanders brought seven thousand men; Jirhalang charged the line, won a great victory, and received an imperial horse.

sentences.zh: 九月，圍錦州，設伏城南，敵不進，追擊破之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he besieged Jinzhou, set an ambush south of the city; the enemy would not advance, and pursuing he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he besieged Jinzhou, ambushed south of the city, and when the enemy hung back he pursued and routed them.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，復圍錦州，立八營，掘壕築塹，以困祖大壽。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year he again besieged Jinzhou, set up eight camps, dug trenches and built ramparts to hem in Zu Dashou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year he again besieged Jinzhou with eight camps, trenches, and ramparts to trap Zu Dashou.

sentences.zh: 大壽以蒙古兵守外郛，台吉諾木齊等遣人約獻東關，為大壽所覺，與之戰。

translations.literal: Dashou had Mongol troops guard the outer wall; taiji Nomuci and others sent men to arrange surrender of the east gate, which Dashou discovered and fought them.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou put Mongols on the outer wall; taiji Nomuci tried to open the east gate, was discovered, and fought.

sentences.zh: 濟爾哈朗督兵薄城，蒙古兵縋以入，據其郛。

translations.literal: Jirhalang directed troops against the wall; Mongol soldiers were lowered in by rope and seized the outer suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang pressed the wall; Mongols were lowered in by rope and took the outer suburbs.

sentences.zh: 遷蒙古六千餘人於義州，降明將八十餘。

translations.literal: More than six thousand Mongols were moved to Yizhou and more than eighty Ming officers surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: More than six thousand Mongols were resettled at Yizhou and over eighty Ming officers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 上御篤恭殿宣捷。

translations.literal: The ruler announced victory at the Dugong Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler proclaimed victory at the Dugong Hall.

sentences.zh: 四月，敗明援兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he defeated Ming relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he defeated Ming relief.

sentences.zh: 五月，又敗之，斬級二千。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he defeated them again and beheaded two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he beat them again and took two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 六月，師還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九月，復圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, they again besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the forces once more laid siege to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，洪承疇自松山遣兵夜犯我軍，我軍循壕射之，敵敗去，不得入，盡降其衆。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Hong Chengchou sent troops from Songshan by night to strike our army; our army shot along the trenches, the enemy was defeated and withdrew, could not enter, and all their men surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Hong Chengchou dispatched troops from Songshan in a night attack on the Qing forces. The Qing army fired from behind their trenches, routed the enemy, and prevented them from breaking in; the entire force surrendered.

sentences.zh: 七年，再圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, they again besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Jinzhou was besieged again.

sentences.zh: 三月，大壽降，隳松山、塔山、杏山三城以歸，賜鞍馬一、蟒緞百。

translations.literal: In the third month, Dashou surrendered; the three cities of Songshan, Tashan, and Xingshan were dismantled and returned, and he was granted one saddle horse and one hundred python robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zu Dashou surrendered. Songshan, Tashan, and Xingshan were razed and restored to Qing control, and Dashou received one saddle horse and a hundred python-patterned silks.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖即位，命與睿親王多爾袞同輔政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Shizu ascended the throne, he was ordered to assist in government together with Prince Rui Dorgon.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after the Shunzhi Emperor took the throne, Jirhalang was appointed to serve as co-regent alongside Prince Rui Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 九月，攻寧遠，拔中後所，並取中前所。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, they attacked Ningyuan, captured Zhonghousuo, and also took Zhongqiansuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the army attacked Ningyuan, seized Zhonghousuo, and took Zhongqiansuo as well.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，王令政事先白睿親王，列銜亦先之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, the prince was ordered that in government affairs he should first inform Prince Rui, and in joint signatures his name should come first.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, the prince was instructed to consult Prince Rui Dorgon before acting on policy and to list his own name ahead of Dorgon's on joint documents.

sentences.zh: 五月，睿親王率師入山海關，定京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Prince Rui led the army through Shanhaiguan and secured the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Prince Rui Dorgon marched through Shanhaiguan and established control over Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十月，封為信義輔政叔王，賜金千、銀萬、緞千疋。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he was enfeoffed as Prince Uncle Assisting Government of Faithful Righteousness, and granted a thousand taels of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, and a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, he was created Prince Uncle of Faithful Righteousness Assisting the Regency and rewarded with a thousand taels of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, and a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，以府第逾制，罰銀二千，罷輔政。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, because his residence exceeded prescribed standards, he was fined two thousand taels of silver and removed from the regency.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, his mansion was found to violate building regulations; he was fined two thousand taels of silver and dismissed from the regency.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，貝子屯齊、尚善、屯齊喀等訐王諸罪狀，言王當太宗初喪，不舉發大臣謀立肅親王豪格。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, Beizi Tunqi, Shangshan, Tunqika, and others denounced the prince on various counts, saying that when Taizong had just died, he had not exposed the great ministers' plot to install Prince Su Hooge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year, Beizi Tunqi, Shangshan, Tunqika, and others accused the prince of multiple offenses, charging that at Hong Taiji's death he had failed to reveal a senior ministers' scheme to enthrone Prince Su Hooge.

sentences.zh: 召王就質，議罪當死，遂興大獄。

translations.literal: The prince was summoned to answer the charges; deliberation fixed the penalty at death, and a great prosecution was launched.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang was called in to face interrogation; the court judged him deserving of death and opened a major purge.

sentences.zh: 勳臣額亦都、費英東、揚古利諸子侄皆連染，議罪當死，籍沒。

translations.literal: The sons and nephews of meritorious ministers Eidu, Feiyingdong, and Yangguli were all implicated; deliberation fixed the penalty at death and confiscation of property.
translations.idiomatic: The sons and nephews of the meritorious ministers Eidu, Feiyingdong, and Yangguli were drawn into the case as well; all were sentenced to death and their estates were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 既，改從輕比，王坐降郡王，肅親王豪格遂以幽死。

translations.literal: Thereafter the sentence was reduced to a lighter grade; the prince was demoted to Prince of a Commandery, and Prince Su Hooge thereupon died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: The punishments were later mitigated. Jirhalang was reduced to commandery-prince rank, and Prince Su Hooge was left to die in secret imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 閏四月，復親王爵。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month, his princely rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month, he was restored to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 九月，命為定遠大將軍，率師下湖廣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he was appointed Grand General Defending the Distance and ordered to lead the army south into Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he was named Grand General Defending the Distance and sent to lead an expedition into Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十月，次山東，降將劉澤清以叛誅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the army halted in Shandong; the surrendered general Liu Zeqing was executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, the army paused in Shandong, where the turncoat general Liu Zeqing was put to death for treason.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，次長沙，明總督何騰蛟，總兵馬進忠、陶養用等，合李自成餘部一隻虎等據湖南。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, the army halted at Changsha; Ming Governor-General He Tengjiao, generals Ma Jinzhong and Tao Yangyong, and others, together with the One Tiger remnant band of Li Zicheng, held Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year, the army encamped at Changsha. Ming Governor-General He Tengjiao, generals Ma Jinzhong and Tao Yangyong, and Li Zicheng's surviving follower known as the One Tiger jointly held Hunan.

sentences.zh: 王分軍進擊，拔湘潭，擒騰蛟。

translations.literal: The prince divided his army to advance and attack, captured Xiangtan, and seized He Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang split his forces and pressed the attack, took Xiangtan, and captured He Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 四月，次辰州，一隻虎遁走，克寶慶，破南山坡、大水、洪江諸路兵凡二十八營。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the army halted at Chenzhou; the One Tiger fled, Baoding was taken, and twenty-eight enemy camps on the routes of Nanshanpo, Dashui, and Hongjiang were broken.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, the army stopped at Chenzhou. The One Tiger escaped, Baoding fell, and twenty-eight enemy camps along the Nanshanpo, Dashui, and Hongjiang routes were overrun.

sentences.zh: 七月，下靖州，進攻衡州，斬養用。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Jingzhou was taken; an attack was pressed on Hengzhou, and Tao Yangyong was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Jingzhou was captured and Hengzhou besieged; Tao Yangyong was executed.

sentences.zh: 逐敵至廣西全州，分軍下道州、黎平及烏撒土司，先後克六十餘城。

translations.literal: Pursuing the enemy to Quanzhou in Guangxi, he divided the army to take Daozhou, Liping, and the Wusa chieftaincy, successively capturing more than sixty cities.
translations.idiomatic: Driving the enemy as far as Quanzhou in Guangxi, he detached columns to seize Daozhou, Liping, and the Wusa native domain, taking more than sixty towns in succession.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，師還，賜金二百、銀二萬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, the army returned, and he was granted two hundred taels of gold and twenty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, the army returned home, and he received two hundred taels of gold and twenty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，偕巽親王滿達海、端重親王博洛、敬謹親王尼堪奏削故睿親王多爾袞爵，語詳睿親王傳。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year, together with Prince Xun Mandahai, Prince Duanzhong Boluo, and Prince Jingjin Nikan, he memorialized to strip the late Prince Rui Dorgon of his title; the details are given in the biography of Prince Rui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year, he joined Princes Mandahai, Boluo, and Nikan in a memorial calling for the posthumous stripping of Prince Rui Dorgon's titles; the full account appears in Dorgon's biography.

sentences.zh: 三月，以王老，免朝賀、謝恩行禮。

translations.literal: In the third month, because the prince was old, he was exempted from court congratulations and thanksgiving ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on account of his advanced age, the prince was excused from attending congratulatory and thanksgiving audiences.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，進封叔和碩鄭親王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year, he was advanced to Prince Uncle and Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year, he was promoted to Uncle Prince of the First Rank and Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，疏言：「太祖創業之初，日與四大貝勒、五大臣討論政事得失，咨訪士民疾苦，上下交孚，鮮有壅蔽，故能掃清清雄，肇興大業。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year, he submitted a memorial saying: "At the beginning of Taizu's founding enterprise, each day he discussed with the Four Great Beile and Five Great Ministers the gains and losses of government, inquired into the hardships of scholars and commoners, and upper and lower were in mutual trust with little obstruction; thus he was able to sweep away rival heroes and inaugurate the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year, he submitted a memorial stating: "When Taizu first founded the dynasty, he daily debated policy with the Four Great Beile and Five Great Ministers, sought out the people's grievances, and kept court and country in close accord with few barriers to truth. That is how he cleared away his rivals and laid the foundations of the state.

sentences.zh: 太宗纘承大統，亦時與諸王貝勒講論不輟，崇獎忠直，錄功棄過，凡詔令必求可以順民心、垂久遠者。

translations.literal: Taizong inherited the great succession and likewise unceasingly debated with the various princes and beile, honored loyalty and straight speech, recorded merit and overlooked faults, and in every edict sought what could accord with the people's hearts and endure for long ages.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, inheriting the throne, also held constant counsel with the princes and beile, rewarded the loyal and outspoken, weighed merit above fault, and drafted every edict to win the people's trust and stand the test of time.

sentences.zh: 又慮武備廢弛，時出射獵，諸王貝勒置酒高宴，以優戲為樂。

translations.literal: He also feared that military readiness would fall into neglect, and so from time to time went out hunting and shooting; the various princes and beile set out wine and held grand feasts, taking comic entertainments as their pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that martial discipline might slacken, he still went hunting from time to time; meanwhile the princes and beile held lavish banquets and amused themselves with comic performances.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒曰：『我國肇興，治弓矢，繕甲兵，視將士若赤子，故人爭效死，每戰必克。

translations.literal: Taizong angrily said: 'When our state first rose, we tended bows and arrows, repaired armor and weapons, and treated soldiers like our own children; therefore men competed to die for us, and every battle was won.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong angrily said: "When our dynasty first arose, we kept our bows strung, maintained our armor, and treated our troops like our own children. That is why men fought to the death for us and every battle ended in victory.

sentences.zh: 常恐後世子孫棄淳厚之風，沿習漢俗，即於慆淫。

translations.literal: I constantly fear that later generations and descendants will abandon our plain and honest ways, follow Han customs, and thereby fall into dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: I have always feared that our descendants would abandon our plain, hardy ways, adopt Han habits, and sink into indulgence.

sentences.zh: 今若輩為此荒樂，欲國家隆盛，其可得乎？』

translations.literal: Now if you people pursue such wasteful pleasures, how can you expect the state to flourish?'
translations.idiomatic: If you now waste yourselves in such pleasures, how can the realm ever prosper?"

sentences.zh: 遣大臣索尼再三申諭。

translations.literal: He sent the great minister Sonin repeatedly to admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the senior minister Sonin again and again to deliver the warning.

sentences.zh: 今皇上詔大小臣工盡言，臣以為平治天下，莫要於信。

translations.literal: Now the Emperor has ordered officials great and small to speak freely; your subject holds that in governing the realm, nothing is more essential than trust.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has invited officials at every level to speak openly, I believe that nothing matters more in governing the empire than credibility.

sentences.zh: 前者軫恤滿洲官民，聞者懽忭。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Manchu officials and people were shown imperial concern, those who heard of it rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty recently showed concern for Manchu officials and commoners, the announcement was met with widespread rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 嗣役修乾清宮，詔令不信，何以使民？

translations.literal: Later, when corvée labor was imposed to repair the Qianqing Palace, the edict was not believed—how then can the people be governed?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when corvée was levied to repair the Qianqing Palace, the earlier pledge lost the people's trust. How can subjects be ruled when edicts are not believed?

sentences.zh: 伏祈效法太祖、太宗，時與大臣詳究政事得失，必商榷盡善，然後布之詔令，庶幾法行民信，紹二聖之休烈。

translations.literal: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will follow the example of Taizu and Taizong, frequently discuss with great ministers in detail the gains and losses of government, deliberating until all is perfected before issuing edicts, so that laws may be enforced and the people may trust, continuing the glorious achievements of the two sages.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to follow Taizu and Taizong's example: consult senior ministers often, refine policy in full deliberation, and only then promulgate edicts, so that law may be enforced, the people may believe, and the achievements of the two founding sages may be carried forward.

sentences.zh: 抑有請者，垂謨昭德，莫先于史。

translations.literal: I also have a further request: in handing down models and displaying virtue, nothing comes before history.
translations.idiomatic: I have one further request: to transmit exemplary rule and display virtue, nothing precedes the keeping of history.

sentences.zh: 古聖明王，進君子，遠小人，措天下于太平，垂鴻名于萬世，繄史官是賴。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings advanced the worthy and kept the petty at a distance, set the realm in peace, and left a great name for ten thousand generations—all this depended on the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity promoted the worthy, kept flatterers at bay, brought the realm to peace, and left their names for ten thousand generations—always with the historiographers as their support.

sentences.zh: 今宜設起居注官，置之左右，一言一行，傳之無窮，亦治道之助也。」

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to establish diarists and place them at the sovereign's side, so that every word and act may be transmitted without end; this too would aid the way of governance."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should appoint diarists to attend at court, so that every word and deed may be preserved for posterity. That too would strengthen good government."

sentences.zh: 疏上，嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 五月，疾革，上臨問，奏：「臣受三朝厚恩，未及答，原以取雲貴，殄桂王，統一四海為念。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month, when his illness became critical, the Emperor came in person to inquire; he memorialized: "Your subject has received thick grace from three reigns and has not yet repaid it; I wish only to take the capture of Yunnan and Guizhou, the destruction of the Prince of Gui, and the unification of the four seas as my concern."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, as his illness turned grave, the Emperor visited him in person. Jirhalang replied: "I have received boundless favor across three reigns and have not yet repaid it. My only wish is to see Yunnan and Guizhou taken, the Prince of Gui destroyed, and the four seas united under one rule."

sentences.zh: 上垂涕曰：「天奈何不令朕叔長年耶！」

translations.literal: The Emperor, with tears falling, said: "Why will Heaven not grant my uncle long years!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept and said: "Why will Heaven not grant my uncle a long life!"

sentences.zh: 言已，大慟。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he was overcome with great grief.
translations.idiomatic: Having spoken, he was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 命工圖其像。

translations.literal: He ordered artisans to paint his portrait.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered artists to paint Jirhalang's portrait.

sentences.zh: 翌日薨，年五十七。

translations.literal: The next day he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following day, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 輟朝七日。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for seven days of mourning.

sentences.zh: 賜銀萬，置守園十戶，立碑紀功。

translations.literal: Ten thousand taels of silver were granted, ten households were assigned to guard the tomb park, and a stele was erected to record his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand taels of silver were granted, ten households were assigned to maintain his tomb park, and a stele was erected to commemorate his achievements.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年六月，追諡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Kangxi, a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Kangxi 10, a posthumous title was conferred upon him.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年正月，詔配享太廟，復嗣王封號曰鄭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-third year of Qianlong, an edict ordered him granted posthumous sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and restoration of the hereditary princely title as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 43, an edict granted him posthumous worship in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and restored the hereditary princely title of Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 濟爾哈朗子十一，有爵者四：富爾敦、濟度、勒度、巴爾堪。

translations.literal: Jirhalang had eleven sons; four held noble rank: Furdan, Jidu, Ledu, and Barkhan.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang had eleven sons, of whom four held noble titles: Furdan, Jidu, Ledu, and Barkhan.

sentences.zh: 富爾敦，濟爾哈朗第一子，封世子。

translations.literal: Furdan, the first son of Jirhalang, was enfeoffed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Furdan, Jirhalang's eldest son, was created heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，卒，諡悫厚。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, he died; his posthumous title was Sincere and Generous.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shunzhi 8 and was posthumously titled Sincere and Generous.

sentences.zh: 簡純親王濟度，濟爾哈朗第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Jianchun Jidu was the second son of Jirhalang.
translations.idiomatic: Jidu, Prince Jianchun, was Jirhalang's second son.

sentences.zh: 初封簡郡王。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of a Commandery of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Commandery Prince of Jian.

sentences.zh: 富爾敦卒，封世子。

translations.literal: When Furdan died, he was enfeoffed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Furdan's death, he was made heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月，命為定遠大將軍，率師討鄭成功。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year, he was appointed Grand General Defending the Distance and ordered to lead the army against Zheng Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year, he was named Grand General Defending the Distance and sent to lead an expedition against Zheng Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 十二年九月，次福州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twelfth year, the army halted at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twelfth year, the army encamped at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，進次泉州。

translations.literal: After some time, he advanced and halted at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, he moved forward and encamped at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月，成功將黃梧、蘇明、鄭純自海澄來降，移軍次漳州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year, Chenggong's generals Huang Wu, Su Ming, and Zheng Chun surrendered from Haicheng; the army moved and halted at Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year, Zheng Chenggong's generals Huang Wu, Su Ming, and Zheng Chun defected from Haicheng, and the army shifted camp to Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄，成功犯福州，遣梅勒額真阿克善等赴援，擊敗之，斬二百餘級。

translations.literal: Soon Chenggong attacked Fuzhou; he dispatched Meile Ejen Akshan and others to the relief, defeated the enemy, and beheaded more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zheng Chenggong attacked Fuzhou. Jidu sent Meile Ejen Akshan and others to reinforce the city, routed the enemy, and killed more than two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 復擊斬其將林祖蘭等，奪其舟十有四。

translations.literal: He again attacked and beheaded their general Lin Zulan and others, and seized fourteen of their boats.
translations.idiomatic: In a further engagement he killed the enemy general Lin Zulan and others and captured fourteen of their vessels.

sentences.zh: 又分軍攻惠安、閩安、漳浦，獲舟數百，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: He also divided the army to attack Huian, Min'an, and Zhangpu, capturing several hundred boats and beheading more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent detachments against Huian, Min'an, and Zhangpu, seizing several hundred boats and killing more than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，師還，上遣大臣迎勞盧溝橋，始聞鄭獻親王之喪，令入就喪次，上臨其第慰諭之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year, the army returned; the Emperor sent great ministers to welcome and congratulate him at Lugou Bridge. Only then did he learn of the mourning for Prince Xian of Zheng; he was ordered to enter and attend the mourning rites, and the Emperor came in person to his residence to console him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year, the army returned. The Emperor dispatched senior ministers to welcome him at Lugou Bridge, where Jidu first learned of Prince Jirhalang's death. He was ordered to enter the capital for the mourning rites, and the Emperor visited his residence in person to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 五月，襲爵，改號簡親王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he inherited the title and changed his designation to Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, he succeeded to the title and was redesignated Prince of Jian.

sentences.zh: 十七年，薨。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year.

sentences.zh: 濟度子五，喇布、德塞、雅布先後襲爵簡親王。

translations.literal: Jidu had five sons; Labu, Desai, and Yabu successively inherited the title of Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Jidu had five sons; Labu, Desai, and Yabu each inherited the title of Prince of Jian in turn.

sentences.zh: 喇布，濟度第二子。

translations.literal: Labu was the second son of Jidu.
translations.idiomatic: Labu was Jidu's second son.

sentences.zh: 濟度初薨，以第三子德塞襲。

translations.literal: When Jidu first died, the third son Desai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Jidu first died, his third son Desai succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，薨，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, he died; his posthumous title was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Desai died in Kangxi 9 and was posthumously titled Hui.

sentences.zh: 是年，喇布襲爵。

translations.literal: In that same year, Labu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Labu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，十三年九月，命為揚威大將軍，率師駐江寧。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, in the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was appointed Grand General Displaying Might and ordered to lead the army stationed at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui rebelled, Labu was appointed Grand General Displaying Might in the ninth month of the thirteenth year and stationed his army at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十四年九月，移師江西，鎮南昌，屢遣兵援東鄉，擊鄱陽，破金谿、萬年。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year, he moved the army to Jiangxi and garrisoned Nanchang, repeatedly dispatching troops to relieve Dongxiang, attacking Poyang, and breaking Jinxi and Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year, he transferred his forces to Jiangxi, garrisoned Nanchang, repeatedly sent troops to relieve Dongxiang, attacked Poyang, and captured Jinxi and Wannian.

sentences.zh: 三桂將高得捷、韓大任陷吉安，詔趣進師。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's generals Gao Dejie and Han Daren captured Ji'an; an edict urgently ordered him to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's generals Gao Dejie and Han Daren took Ji'an, and the court urgently ordered Labu to advance.

sentences.zh: 喇布駐南昌，不出師攻吉安，屯螺子山，敵來攻，師敗績。

translations.literal: Labu remained at Nanchang and did not march out to attack Ji'an; he encamped at Luozi Mountain, the enemy came to attack, and the army suffered a defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Labu stayed in Nanchang and failed to march against Ji'an. He encamped at Luozi Mountain; when the enemy attacked, his army was routed.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎班迪按敗狀，喇布乃督師圍吉安。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Vice Minister Bandi to investigate the defeat; only then did Labu personally direct the army in besieging Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Vice Minister Bandi to investigate the defeat, after which Labu at last took personal command of the siege of Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月，敵引走，喇布入吉安，疏稱大任等屯寧都請降，詔報可。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixteenth year, the enemy withdrew; Labu entered Ji'an and memorialized that Han Daren and others at Ningdu requested surrender; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixteenth year, the enemy withdrew. Labu entered Ji'an and reported that Han Daren and others at Ningdu were offering surrender; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 既而大任自寧都出擾萬安、泰和，喇布復請增兵。

translations.literal: Thereafter Han Daren came out from Ningdu and raided Wan'an and Taihe; Labu again requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Han Daren sallied from Ningdu and raided Wan'an and Taihe, and Labu again asked for more troops.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「簡親王喇布自至江西，無尺寸之功，深居會城，虛糜廩餉。

translations.literal: The Emperor admonished him, saying: "Prince of Jian Labu, since arriving in Jiangxi, has achieved not the slightest merit, dwelling deep within the provincial capital and wastefully consuming rations and pay.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him: "Since Prince of Jian Labu reached Jiangxi, he has won not a single achievement. He has remained shut up in the provincial capital, wasting grain and pay.

sentences.zh: 迨赴吉安，以重兵圍城，而韓大任竄逸，竊踞寧都，復擾萬安、泰和，不能擊滅。

translations.literal: When he finally went to Ji'an, though he surrounded the city with a large force, Han Daren slipped away, secretly held Ningdu, and again harassed Wan'an and Taihe, yet could not be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally moved on Ji'an, he invested the city with a large army yet let Han Daren escape, hold Ningdu, and resume raids on Wan'an and Taihe without being able to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 喇布所轄官兵為數不為少，乃一大任不能翦除，宜嚴加處分，俟事平日議罪。」

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers under Labu's command are not few in number; that he could not eliminate even Han Daren warrants severe punishment, to be deliberated after affairs are settled."
translations.idiomatic: The troops under Labu's command are hardly insufficient; that he could not eliminate even Han Daren warrants severe punishment, to be decided once the campaign is over."

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，護軍統領哈克三等敗大任於老虎洞，毀其壘，斬六千級。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year, Guard Commander Hakesan and others defeated Han Daren at Laohudong, destroyed his fortifications, and beheaded six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year, Guard Commander Hakesan and others defeated Han Daren at Laohudong, destroyed his fortifications, and killed six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 大任奔福建，詣康親王傑書軍降。

translations.literal: Han Daren fled to Fujian and surrendered to the army of Prince Kang Jieshu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren fled to Fujian and surrendered to Prince Kang Jieshu's army.

sentences.zh: 二月，移師湖南，駐茶陵。

translations.literal: In the second month, he moved the army to Hunan and garrisoned Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Labu transferred his army to Hunan and garrisoned Chaling.

sentences.zh: 八月，三桂死於衡州，詔令自安仁進師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wu Sangui died at Hengzhou; an edict ordered him to advance from Anren.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wu Sangui died at Hengzhou, and an edict ordered Labu to advance from Anren.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，進復衡州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year, he advanced and recovered Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighteenth year, he advanced and recaptured Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，分軍復祁陽、耒陽、寶慶。

translations.literal: In the second month, he divided the army to recover Qiyang, Leiyang, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, he sent detachments to retake Qiyang, Leiyang, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 九月，進次廣西，駐桂林。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he advanced and halted in Guangxi, garrisoning Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he moved into Guangxi and garrisoned Guilin.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，馬承廕以柳州叛。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year, Ma Chengyin rebelled at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the nineteenth year, Ma Chengyin rebelled at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，進攻柳州，承廕降。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he advanced to attack Liuzhou, and Ma Chengyin surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, he advanced against Liuzhou, and Ma Chengyin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 八月，移駐南寧。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he moved his garrison to Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, he shifted his garrison to Nanning.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔選所部付大將軍賚塔進攻雲南。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict selected troops from his command and assigned them to Grand General Laita for the attack on Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, an edict detached part of his force and placed it under Grand General Laita for the campaign against Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 二十年八月，召還京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twentieth year, he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twentieth year, he was recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十月，薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，追論吉安失機罪，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, his failure at Ji'an was reviewed posthumously and his title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, he was posthumously condemned for missing the opportunity at Ji'an and stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 雅布，濟度第五子。

translations.literal: Yabu was the fifth son of Jidu.
translations.idiomatic: Yabu was Jidu's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，襲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the title in the twenty-second year.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，命赴蘇尼特防噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was ordered to go to Sunite to guard against Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, he was ordered to Sunite to guard against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，噶爾丹深入烏珠穆沁地，以恭親王常甯為安北大將軍，雅布與信郡王鄂扎副之，出喜峰口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, when Galdan penetrated deep into Ujimchin territory, Prince Gong Changning was appointed Grand General Pacifying the North, with Yabu and Prince Xin Ezhai as his deputies; they marched out through Xifengkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, when Galdan pushed deep into Ujimchin territory, Prince Gong Changning was appointed Grand General Pacifying the North, with Yabu and Prince Xin Ezhai as his deputies; the army marched out through Xifengkou.

sentences.zh: 既而罷行，詔赴裕親王福全軍參贊軍務。

translations.literal: Soon after, the march was cancelled; an edict ordered him to go to Prince Yu Fuquan's army to assist and comment on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition was soon called off, and he was ordered to join Prince Fuquan's army as a staff officer for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 八月，擊敗噶爾丹于烏闌布通，噶爾丹遁，未窮追。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Galdan was defeated at Ulan Butong; Galdan fled, and he was not pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they defeated Galdan at Ulan Butong; Galdan escaped, and the enemy was not pursued to extinction.

sentences.zh: 師還，議不追敵罪，當奪爵，詔罰俸三年。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the offense of not pursuing the enemy was debated; deprivation of rank was due, but an edict fined salary for three years.
translations.idiomatic: After the army came home, failure to pursue the enemy was debated and would normally have cost him his title; instead an edict reduced his stipend for three years.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從上親征。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, he followed the emperor on a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he accompanied the emperor on campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，掌宗人府事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he took charge of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he was placed in charge of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 四十年，薨，諡曰修。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he died; the posthumous title was Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fortieth year and was given the posthumous name Xiu.

sentences.zh: 子十五，雅爾江阿、神保住先後襲爵。

translations.literal: He had fifteen sons; Yarjiang'a and Shen Baozhu successively inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He had fifteen sons; Yarjiang'a and Shen Baozhu inherited the princedom in turn.

sentences.zh: 雅爾江阿，雅布第一子。

translations.literal: Yarjiang'a was Yabu's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Yarjiang'a was Yabu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 初封世子。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made heir to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，襲。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，詔責雅爾江阿躭飲廢事，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, an edict rebuked Yarjiang'a for indulging in drink and neglecting duty, and stripped him of his rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Yongzheng reign an edict condemned Yarjiang'a for heavy drinking and neglect of office and removed his title.

sentences.zh: 神保住，雅布第十四子。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhu was Yabu's fourteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhu was Yabu's fourteenth son.

sentences.zh: 初封鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a Defender General of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was first granted the rank of Defender General of the State.

sentences.zh: 雅爾江阿既黜，世宗命襲爵。

translations.literal: After Yarjiang'a was deposed, the Shizong Emperor ordered him to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Yarjiang'a was removed, the Yongzheng Emperor ordered Shen Baozhu to succeed to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，詔責神保住恣意妄為，致兩目成眚，又虐待兄女，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, an edict rebuked Shen Baozhu for acting willfully, causing blindness in both eyes, and cruelly mistreating his elder brother's daughter, and stripped him of his rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Qianlong reign an edict condemned Shen Baozhu for reckless conduct that left him blind in both eyes and for abusing his elder brother's daughter, and his title was taken away.

sentences.zh: 以濟爾哈朗弟貝勒費揚武曾孫德沛襲。

translations.literal: De Pei, a great-great-grandson of Jirhalang's younger brother, Beile Feiyangwu, was made to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: The succession passed to De Pei, a great-great-grandson of Jirhalang's younger brother, Prince Feiyangwu.

sentences.zh: 德沛字濟齋，貝子福存子。

translations.literal: De Pei, style Jizhai, was the son of Beizi Fucun.
translations.idiomatic: De Pei, whose style was Jizhai, was the son of Beizi Fucun.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，授鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng he was appointed Defender General of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Yongzheng reign he was made Defender General of the State.

sentences.zh: 以果親王允禮薦，世宗召見，問所欲，對曰：「原廁孔廡分特豚之饋。」

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Prince Guo Yunli, the Shizong Emperor summoned him, asked what he wished, and he replied: 'I would be content to share in the special pig offering divided at the Confucian temple slaughter stall.'
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Prince Guo Yunli, he was summoned by the Yongzheng Emperor, who asked what post he wanted; he answered that he would be satisfied with a humble share of the sacrificial meat apportioned at the temple slaughter stalls.

sentences.zh: 上大重之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，改古北口提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was transferred to be commander at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign he was made commander at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 二年，授甘肅巡撫，奏言：「甘肅州縣多在萬山中，遇災，民入城領賑，路窎遠。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Governor of Gansu and memorialized: 'In Gansu, prefectures and counties lie mostly deep in ten-thousand-li mountains; when disaster strikes, the people enter the cities to draw relief, and the roads are long and remote.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became governor of Gansu and reported that most Gansu districts lay in rugged mountains, so when famine struck peasants had to travel far into walled towns for grain, which was impractical.

sentences.zh: 宜於鄉鎮設廠散糧，並許州縣吏具詳即施賑。」

translations.literal: Relief grain should be distributed at depots in townships and market towns, and county and prefectural clerks should be allowed to submit details and grant relief on the spot.'
translations.idiomatic: He proposed setting up rural granaries and letting local officials disburse aid at once on verified petition.

sentences.zh: 旋擢湖廣總督，奏言：「治苗疆宜勸墾田，置學校，並諭令植樹。」

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted Governor-General of Huguang and memorialized: 'To govern the Miao frontier one should encourage reclaiming fields, establish schools, and order tree planting.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon promoted to governor-general of Huguang, he urged that the Miao country be settled by promoting farming, founding schools, and requiring tree planting.

sentences.zh: 四年，調閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to the Fujian–Zhejiang governor-generalship.

sentences.zh: 御史朱續晫劾福建巡撫王士任贓私，上疑不實，命續晫會鞫。

translations.literal: The censor Zhu Xupu impeached Fujian Governor Wang Shiren for corruption; the emperor doubted the charge was true and ordered Zhu Xupu to join in the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhu Xupu accused Fujian governor Wang Shiren of graft; the throne doubted the case and sent Zhu Xupu to sit in joint inquiry.

sentences.zh: 德沛自承失察，直續晫而奪士任官，時服其公。

translations.literal: De Pei himself admitted failure of supervision, sided with Zhu Xupu, and stripped Wang Shiren of office; at the time people admired his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: De Pei confessed to lax oversight, backed Zhu Xupu, and removed Wang Shiren from office, winning public respect for his impartiality.

sentences.zh: 福州將軍隆升貪縱，劾去之。

translations.literal: The Fuzhou General Long Sheng was greedy and unrestrained; he was impeached and removed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and dismissed the Fuzhou general Long Sheng for greed and license.

sentences.zh: 奏，宜酌移鎮將營汛，預弭爭端。」

translations.literal: He memorialized that garrison generals' camps and posts should be judiciously shifted to forestall disputes in advance.'
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that frontier garrisons be redeployed with care to prevent clashes before they arose.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，諭曰：「德沛屢任封晫言；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year an edict said: 'De Pei, having repeatedly held frontier posts, speaks frankly;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year the throne declared that De Pei, who had served repeatedly on the frontiers, was outspoken in counsel;

sentences.zh: 「海濱居民恆械疆，操守廉潔，一介不取，逋負日積，致蠲舊產。

translations.literal: 'on the coast the people constantly take up arms in feud; he is upright and incorrupt, accepts not a single thing, yet debts mount daily until he has had to sell his old property.
translations.idiomatic: that though coastal society was rife with armed feuds, he remained scrupulously honest, took no gifts, and still sank so deep in debt that he had to part with his family holdings.

sentences.zh: 賜福建籓庫銀一萬，以風有位。」

translations.literal: 'Ten thousand taels from the Fujian provincial treasury are granted to set an example for those in office.'
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand taels from the Fujian treasury were bestowed on him as a model for officials.

sentences.zh: 六年，兼署浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he also served concurrently as Governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he additionally acted as governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 七年，調兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Governor-General of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was moved to the Liangjiang governor-generalship.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚大水，令府縣發倉庫，奏撥地丁、關稅、鹽課銀十萬兩治賑。

translations.literal: Great floods struck Huai and Yang; he ordered prefectures and counties to open granaries and memorialized an allocation of one hundred thousand taels from land tax, customs duties, and salt levies for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai–Yang region flooded, he opened local granaries and secured a hundred thousand taels from land tax, customs, and salt revenues for relief.

sentences.zh: 尋議河事與高斌不合。

translations.literal: Soon he differed with Gao Bin over river works.
translations.idiomatic: He soon clashed with Gao Bin over hydraulic policy.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月，署山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twelfth year he acted as Governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twelfth year he served as acting governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，擢吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was promoted Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十三年七月，以疾解任。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year he was relieved because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 神保住既黜，上以德沛操履厚重，特命襲爵，曾祖貝勒費揚武、祖貝子傅喇塔、父福存，並追封簡親王。

translations.literal: After Shen Baozhu was deposed, the emperor, because De Pei's conduct was weighty and solid, specially ordered him to inherit the title; his great-grandfather Beile Feiyangwu, grandfather Beizi Fulata, and father Fucun were all posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Baozhu was removed, the emperor singled out De Pei for his steady character and made him prince, posthumously raising his great-grandfather Feiyangwu, grandfather Fulata, and father Fucun to Prince Jian.

sentences.zh: 十七年，薨，諡曰儀。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; the posthumous title was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year and was posthumously named Yi.

sentences.zh: 以濟爾哈朗曾孫奇通阿襲。

translations.literal: Jirhalang's great-great-grandson Qitong'a inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to Qitong'a, a great-great-grandson of Jirhalang.

sentences.zh: 奇通阿，輔國公巴賽子。

translations.literal: Qitong'a was the son of Assistant Duke Basai.
translations.idiomatic: Qitong'a was the son of Assistant Duke Basai.

sentences.zh: 初授輔國將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Assistant General of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made Assistant General of the State.

sentences.zh: 襲輔國公。

translations.literal: He inherited as Assistant Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the rank of assistant duke.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，授正紅旗滿州都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was appointed commander of the Manchu Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign he was made commander of the Plain Red Banner Manchus.

sentences.zh: 三年，授領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed grand minister of the imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 十七年，襲。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 祖輔國公巴爾堪、父巴賽，並追封簡親王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Assistant Duke Ba'erkan and father Basai were both posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ba'erkan and father Basai were posthumously raised to Prince Jian.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，掌宗人府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he took charge of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was placed in charge of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，薨，諡曰勤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died; the posthumous title was Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year and was posthumously named Qin.

sentences.zh: 子豐訥亨襲。

translations.literal: His son Fengneheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengneheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 豐訥亨初授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: Fengneheng was at first appointed a third-rank imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Fengneheng was first made a third-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 事高宗，從師討準噶爾，將健銳千人屯呼爾璊。

translations.literal: Serving the Gaozong Emperor, he followed the army against the Zunghars and led a thousand picked Elite Vanguard troops stationed at Hurman.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qianlong Emperor he campaigned against the Zunghars and commanded a thousand Elite Vanguard troops posted at Hurman.

sentences.zh: 霍集占以五千人來犯，合諸軍擊却之，逐北十餘里。

translations.literal: Hojijan came with five thousand men to attack; joining the other forces he drove them back and pursued north more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: When Hojijan attacked with five thousand men, Fengneheng joined the allied forces, repulsed them, and chased them northward for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 師進，敵踞塹以拒戰，奪塹，所乘馬中創，易馬再進，敗敵沁達勒河渡口，再敗敵葉爾羌河岸。

translations.literal: As the army advanced, the enemy held trenches to resist; the trenches were taken, his mount was wounded, he changed horses and advanced again, defeated the enemy at the Qindar River crossing, and defeated them again on the banks of the Yarkand River.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance the foe fought from trenches until they were stormed; his horse was hit, he remounted and pressed on, routing the enemy at the Qindar River ford and again on the Yarkand River.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其勇，遷二等侍衛，擢鑲白旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: An edict praised his valor; he was promoted to second-rank bodyguard and to deputy lieutenant-general of the Manchu Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended his bravery, promoting him to second-rank bodyguard and deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 移軍伊犁，授領隊大臣。

translations.literal: The army moved to Ili and he was appointed a column commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the army shifted to Ili he was made a column commander.

sentences.zh: 擊破瑪哈沁及哈薩克部人，收其馬。

translations.literal: He defeated the Mahajin and Kazakh bands and seized their horses.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the Mahajin and Kazakh forces and captured their horses.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，師還，賜雙眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when the army returned, he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, on the army's return, he received the double-eyed peacock plume.

sentences.zh: 遷護軍統領，管健銳營。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commander of the Guards and managed the Elite Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the guards and placed over the Elite Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 授都統，掌宗人府事。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander-in-chief and took charge of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed banner commander and head of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 四十年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he died; the posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fortieth year and was posthumously named Ke.

sentences.zh: 子積哈納，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jihana inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jihana succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 四十三年正月，復號鄭親王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-third year the title Prince of Zheng was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-third year the house was again styled Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，薨，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he died; the posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-ninth year and was posthumously named Gong.

sentences.zh: 子烏爾恭阿，襲。

translations.literal: His son Wergong'a inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wergong'a inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 烏爾恭阿初名佛爾果崇額，襲爵，詔改名。

translations.literal: Wergong'a was at first named Fo'erguochong'e; on inheriting the title an edict ordered the name changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wergong'a was originally named Fo'erguochong'e; when he succeeded, an edict changed his name.

sentences.zh: 道光二十六年，薨，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Daoguang he died; the posthumous title was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-sixth year of the Daoguang reign and was posthumously named Shen.

sentences.zh: 子端華，襲。

translations.literal: His son Duanhua inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duanhua succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 授御前大臣。

translations.literal: He was appointed a Grand Minister in Attendance before the Throne.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a grand minister in attendance before the throne.

sentences.zh: 宣宗崩，受顧命。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong Emperor died, he received the dying entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: On the Daoguang Emperor's death he was named to the regency council.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，迭命為閱兵大臣、右宗正。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor acceded, he was repeatedly appointed to review troops and as Senior Imperial Clan Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xianfeng Emperor he was repeatedly named to inspect troops and to head the imperial clan commission.

sentences.zh: 京師戒嚴，令督察巡防。

translations.literal: When the capital was placed under martial law, he was ordered to supervise patrols and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Beijing was put under martial law he was charged with overseeing patrols and defenses.

sentences.zh: 十年，扈上幸熱河，授領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he accompanied the emperor to Rehe and was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he escorted the emperor to Rehe and was made grand minister of the imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 端華弟肅順用事，文宗崩，再受顧命，與怡親王載垣及肅順等並號「贊襄政務王大臣」。

translations.literal: Duanhua's younger brother Sushun held power; when the Wenzong Emperor died he again received the dying entrustment, and with Prince Yi Zaichun and Sushun and others was styled jointly 'Princes Regent Assisting Government.'
translations.idiomatic: While his younger brother Sushun dominated court affairs, the Xianfeng Emperor on his deathbed again named Duanhua to the regency, and together with Prince Yi Zaichun, Sushun, and others he was titled a 'Prince Assisting Government.'

sentences.zh: 穆宗還京師，詔責端華等專擅跋扈罪，端華坐賜死。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor returned to the capital, an edict blamed Duanhua and others for domineering arrogance; Duanhua was sentenced to death by imperial gift.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tongzhi Emperor came back to Beijing, an edict condemned Duanhua and his fellows for overbearing abuse of power, and Duanhua was granted death.

sentences.zh: 肅順自有傳。

translations.literal: Sushun has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sushun is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 爵降為不入八分輔國公。

translations.literal: The title was reduced to Assistant Duke not entering the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was lowered to an assistant duke outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 同治元年二月，以濟爾哈朗八世孫岳齡襲。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tongzhi, Jirhalang's eighth-generation descendant Yueling inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first Tongzhi year Yueling, eighth in descent from Jirhalang, took the diminished title.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，克復江寧，復還鄭親王世爵，以奇通阿五世孫承志襲。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, when Jiangning was recovered, the Prince of Zheng title was restored, and Chengzhi, fifth-generation descendant of Qitong'a, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, after Nanjing was retaken, the Prince of Zheng was restored and Chengzhi, fifth in descent from Qitong'a, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 承志，輔國公西朗阿子。

translations.literal: Chengzhi was the son of Assistant Duke Xilang'a.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi was the son of Assistant Duke Xilang'a.

sentences.zh: 初襲輔國公。

translations.literal: At first he inherited as Assistant Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He had first held only the rank of assistant duke.

sentences.zh: 既襲王爵，曾祖輔國公經訥亨、祖輔國公伊豐額、父西朗阿，並追封鄭親王，而以嶽齡改襲輔國公。

translations.literal: After he inherited the princedom, his great-grandfather Assistant Duke Jingneheng, grandfather Assistant Duke Yifeng'e, and father Xilang'a were all posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng, while Yueling was shifted to inherit the assistant dukedom.
translations.idiomatic: On becoming prince he had his forebears Jingneheng, Yifeng'e, and Xilang'a posthumously raised to Prince of Zheng, and Yueling was moved down to the assistant dukedom.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，御史劉慶劾承志品行不端，詔令力圖湔濯。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year the censor Liu Qing impeached Chengzhi for misconduct; an edict ordered him to reform himself thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Censor Liu Qing accused Chengzhi of bad character, and the throne told him to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 十一年，坐令護衛玉壽毆殺主事福珣，奪爵，圈禁。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, for ordering his guard Yushou to beat to death Director Fu Xun, he was stripped of his title and confined.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he lost his title and was placed under house arrest for having his guard Yushou kill the director Fu Xun.

sentences.zh: 以積哈納孫慶至襲。

translations.literal: Jihana's grandson Qingzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The succession went to Qingzhi, grandson of Jihana.

sentences.zh: 慶至，奉恩將軍松德嗣子。

translations.literal: Qingzhi was the adopted son of Banner General Songde.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was the adopted heir of Banner General Songde.

sentences.zh: 既襲王爵，松德追封鄭親王。

translations.literal: After he inherited the princedom, Songde was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhi became prince, Songde was posthumously made Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 慶至，光緒四年，薨，諡曰順。

translations.literal: Qingzhi died in the fourth year of Guangxu; the posthumous title was Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi died in the fourth year of the Guangxu reign and was posthumously named Shun.

sentences.zh: 子凱泰，襲。

translations.literal: His son Kaitai inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kaitai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-sixth year.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恪。

translations.literal: The posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Ke.

sentences.zh: 子昭煦，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhaoxu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoxu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 勒度，濟爾哈朗第三子。

translations.literal: Ledu was Jirhalang's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Ledu was the third son of Jirhalang.

sentences.zh: 封敏郡王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Min.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Prince of Min.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died; the posthumous title was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir, and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 輔國武襄公巴爾堪，濟爾哈朗第四子。

translations.literal: Barkhan, Duke Who Assists the State and Embodies Martial Achievement, was the fourth son of Jirhalang.
translations.idiomatic: Barkhan, posthumously Duke of State Assistance and Martial Achievement, was Jirhalang's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初授輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was first appointed assistant duke general.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made an assistant duke of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，吳三桂據湖南，令巴爾堪率師赴兗州，署梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui held Hunan; Barkhan was ordered to lead troops to Yanzhou and was appointed acting meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 Wu Sangui controlled Hunan; Barkhan was sent with troops to Yanzhou and named acting meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 進次江甯，耿精忠遣兵犯徽州，詔巴爾堪進剿。

translations.literal: Advancing to Jiangning, Geng Jingzhong sent troops to attack Huizhou; an edict ordered Barkhan to advance and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: As he moved up to Jiangning, Geng Jingzhong sent forces against Huizhou, and Barkhan was ordered to march against them.

sentences.zh: 九月，次旌德，聞績溪陷，疾趨過徽嶺，破敵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he halted at Jingde; hearing that Jixi had fallen, he hastened past Huiling and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Jingde; learning that Jixi had fallen, he raced over Huiling Pass and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 江甯將軍額楚繼至，合師逐北，斬三千餘級，克徽州。

translations.literal: Jiangning general Echu arrived next; the combined forces drove the enemy north, beheading more than three thousand, and took Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning general Echu came up, and their united force drove the enemy north, killing more than three thousand and recapturing Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 復破敵黟縣董亭橋，進攻婺源。

translations.literal: Again defeating the enemy at Dongting Bridge in Yi County, he advanced to attack Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated the foe at Dongting Bridge in Yi County and pressed on toward Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 復破敵於奇台嶺、于黃茅新嶺，復婺源。

translations.literal: Again defeating the enemy at Qitai Ridge and Huangmao Xin Ridge, he recovered Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After further victories at Qitai Ridge and Huangmao Xin Ridge, he retook Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 進克樂平，擊破叛將陳九傑，乘勝下饒州。

translations.literal: Advancing he took Leping, routed the rebel general Chen Jiujie, and following victory descended on Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Leping, smashed the rebel general Chen Jiujie, and pressed on to take Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，攻萬年石頭街，敵四萬人禦渡口，水陸並進，破五十七營，斬五千級，擒九傑，克安仁，敵焚舟走。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he attacked Shitoujie in Wannian; forty thousand enemy troops defended the crossing; advancing by land and water together, he broke fifty-seven camps, beheaded five thousand ranks, captured Jiujie, took Anren, and the enemy burned their boats and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he assaulted Shitoujie in Wannian, where forty thousand defenders held the crossing. Striking by land and water together, he destroyed fifty-seven camps, killed five thousand men, captured Jiujie, took Anren, and drove the enemy to burn their boats and flee.

sentences.zh: 五月，復貴溪，進略弋陽，攻永豐。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he recovered Guixi, advanced to operate in Yiyang, and attacked Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he retook Guixi, pushed into Yiyang, and attacked Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，敗於螺子山，議奪官。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year he was defeated at Luozi Mountain; deprivation of rank was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year he was defeated at Luozi Mountain, and officials debated stripping him of rank.

sentences.zh: 偕額楚徇廣東。

translations.literal: Together with Echu he conducted operations in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: With Echu he campaigned through Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 九月，戰韶州蓮花山，陷陣，中流矢，裹創力戰，大破敵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he fought at Lianhua Mountain in Shaozhou, fell into the enemy line, was struck by an arrow, wrapped his wound and fought on fiercely, and routed the enemy greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month at Lianhua Mountain in Shaozhou he plunged into the enemy ranks, took an arrow, bound his wound, and fought on until he had shattered the foe.

sentences.zh: 十九年八月，喇布師次廣西，上命以巴爾堪從。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the nineteenth year Labu's army halted in Guangxi; the emperor ordered Barkhan to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the nineteenth year, as Labu's army reached Guangxi, the emperor ordered Barkhan to join him.

sentences.zh: 病作，語固山額真額赫納等曰：「吾不能臨陣而死，今創發，勿令家人以陣亡冒功也。」

translations.literal: Illness came on; he said to gushan ejen Ehena and others: "I could not die facing the battle line; now my wounds have reopened—do not let my family claim merit by pretending I died in battle."
translations.idiomatic: When his illness took hold he told gushan ejen Ehena and the others: "I was denied death on the battlefield; now my wounds have reopened—do not let my family claim the honors due to one killed in action."

sentences.zh: 遂卒於軍。

translations.literal: He then died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp soon after.

sentences.zh: 喪還，上命內大臣輝塞往奠，下部議恤。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, the emperor ordered Inner Court minister Huise to go offer libations, and the matter was referred to the ministries to discuss condolence grants.
translations.idiomatic: When his body was returned, the emperor sent Inner Court minister Huise to offer libations and ordered the ministries to determine posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，追封諡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子巴賽，襲。

translations.literal: His son Basai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Basai inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 輔國襄湣公巴賽，事聖祖，授鑲藍旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: Basai, Duke Who Assists the State and Embodies Mournful Loyalty, served Emperor Shenzu and was appointed vice lieutenant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: Basai, posthumously Duke of State Assistance and Mournful Loyalty, served Kangxi and was made vice lieutenant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner Han Army.

sentences.zh: 從征噶爾丹，遷正紅旗蒙古都統，署黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Galdan, he was transferred to Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner and acted as general of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Galdan he rose to Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner and served as acting general of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，授甯古塔將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, he was appointed general of Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzheng took the throne, he was made general of Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 既，襲爵，召還。

translations.literal: Thereafter he succeeded to the title and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He then inherited his father's title and was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，授振武將軍，軍阿爾台。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was appointed General Who Quells Martial Foes and garrisoned Altai.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 he was named General Who Quells Martial Foes and posted to Altai.

sentences.zh: 五年，當代還，以喀爾喀郡王丹津多爾濟言巴賽治事整飭，命留防。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when his rotation home was due, the Khalkha prince Danjindorji reported that Basai administered affairs in disciplined order, and he was ordered to remain on garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when he was due to rotate home, Khalkha Prince Danjindorji praised Basai's tight discipline, and he was kept on garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 七年，靖邊大將軍傅爾丹率師討噶爾丹策零，授巴賽副將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Grand General Who Pacifies the Border Furdan led an army against Galdan Tsering; Basai was appointed deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Furdan, Grand General Who Pacifies the Border, marched against Galdan Tsering, and Basai was made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，傅爾丹入覲，護大將軍印。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Furdan entered court for audience; Basai guarded the grand general's seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Furdan went to audience at court, Basai held the grand commander's seal.

sentences.zh: 九年，偕傅爾丹駐科布多。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he garrisoned Kobdo together with Furdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he and Furdan camped at Kobdo.

sentences.zh: 六月，噶爾丹策零以三萬人來犯，傅爾丹信間言噶爾丹策零兵寡，遂出師，次庫列圖嶺。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Galdan Tsering came to attack with thirty thousand men; Furdan believed a report that Galdan Tsering's force was small, and so marched out, halting at Kuletu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Galdan Tsering attacked with thirty thousand men; Furdan, trusting a rumor that the enemy was weak, marched out and halted at Kuletu Ridge.

sentences.zh: 敵據險，攻之不克，移軍和通呼爾哈諾爾。

translations.literal: The enemy held the heights; the attack could not succeed, and the army moved to Hotong Hurhanor.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held the high ground; the assault failed, and the army withdrew to Hotong Hurhanor.

sentences.zh: 敵伏山谷，突起截戰，蒙古兵潰，收滿洲兵四千作方營，保輜重，退渡哈爾哈納河。

translations.literal: The enemy lay hidden in the valleys, rose suddenly to intercept the battle, the Mongol troops routed; four thousand Manchu troops were gathered into a square formation to protect the baggage train, and they retreated across the Kharkha River.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy ambushed from the valleys and cut off the fight; the Mongol troops broke, but four thousand Manchu soldiers were formed into a square to protect the baggage and fell back across the Kharkha River.

sentences.zh: 敵追至，傅爾丹還科布多，巴賽與副將軍查弼納率殘兵越嶺至河濱禦敵，沒於陣。

translations.literal: The enemy pursued to the riverbank; Furdan returned to Kobdo, while Basai and Deputy General Zhabina led the remnant troops over the ridge to the riverbank to resist the enemy and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy pressed to the river, Furdan withdrew to Kobdo; Basai and Deputy Commander Zhabina led the survivors over the ridge to hold the riverbank and were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹策零之衆旌黃帶示我師曰：「汝宗室為我所殺矣！」

translations.literal: Galdan Tsering's troops displayed a yellow sash and showed our army, saying: "Your imperial clansmen have been killed by us!"
translations.idiomatic: Galdan Tsering's men waved a yellow sash before our army and cried: "We have killed your imperial kinsmen!"

sentences.zh: 賜恤諡，祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: Condolence grants and a posthumous title were bestowed, and he was enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors were granted, and he was enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 子奇通阿，襲。

translations.literal: His son Qitong'a succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qitong'a inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 尋改襲簡親王，公爵當除。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the succession was changed to the Prince of Simple Directness, and the ducal title was to be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He soon inherited instead as Prince of Simple Directness, and the ducal title was set aside.

sentences.zh: 高宗以巴爾堪、巴賽仍世有戰功，以奇通阿次子經訥亨襲。
