translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, because Barkhan and Basai had generation after generation rendered military merit, had Qitong'a's second son Jingneheng succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Because Barkhan and Basai had served with distinction across generations, the Qianlong emperor had Qitong'a's second son Jingneheng inherit the line.

sentences.zh: 四傳至曾孫承志，復改襲鄭親王。

translations.literal: After four transmissions to great-great-grandson Chengzhi, the succession was again changed to Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations later, when the title passed to great-great-grandson Chengzhi, it reverted to the Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 靖定貝勒費揚武，一名芬古，舒爾哈齊第八子。

translations.literal: Beile of Settled Tranquility Feiyangwu, also named Fenggu, was the eighth son of Shu'erhachi.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyangwu, Beile of Settled Tranquility—also known as Fenggu—was Shu'erhachi's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，授鑲藍旗固山額真。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong he was appointed gushan ejen of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 5 he was made gushan ejen of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 從上伐明，攻大淩河城，費揚武率本旗兵圍其西南。

translations.literal: Following the ruler in an expedition against the Ming, he attacked Dalinghe city; Feiyangwu led his banner troops in besieging the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against the Ming he joined the assault on Dalinghe; Feiyangwu led his banner in the siege of the southwest quarter.

sentences.zh: 上幸阿濟格營，城兵突出，費揚武擊敗之。

translations.literal: The ruler visited Ajige's camp; the city troops sallied forth, and Feiyangwu defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler visited Ajige's camp, the garrison sallied out and Feiyangwu drove them back.

sentences.zh: 上令諸軍向錦州，幟而馳，若明援兵至者，以致祖大壽。

translations.literal: The ruler ordered the armies to advance toward Jinzhou with banners flying and horses galloping as if Ming relief had arrived, to alarm Zu Dashou.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler had the armies ride toward Jinzhou with banners streaming as though Ming reinforcements had come, to frighten Zu Dashou.

sentences.zh: 費揚武迎擊，大壽敗入城，遂不敢出。

translations.literal: Feiyangwu met and attacked them; Dashou was defeated and entered the city, and thereafter did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyangwu met and repulsed them; Dashou fled into the city and never again dared sally forth.

sentences.zh: 八年，再從伐明，師進獨石口，克長安嶺，攻赤城，克其郛。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again followed in an expedition against the Ming; the army advanced to Dushikou, took Chang'an Ridge, attacked Chicheng, and took its outer suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he again joined the Ming campaign; the army entered Dushikou, seized Chang'an Ridge, attacked Chicheng, and took its outer suburbs.

sentences.zh: 九年，師入山西，上命費揚武等攻寧、錦，緩明師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the army entered Shanxi; the ruler ordered Feiyangwu and others to attack Ning and Jin to slow the Ming armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, as the army entered Shanxi, the ruler ordered Feiyangwu and others to strike Ning and Jin to pin down Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 大壽軍大淩河西，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Dashou's army was west of Dalinghe; they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou's army lay west of Dalinghe; Feiyangwu defeated it.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，伐明，克城十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, on an expedition against the Ming, ten cities were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1, on campaign against the Ming, ten cities were captured.

sentences.zh: 是冬，伐朝鮮。

translations.literal: That winter they campaigned against Korea.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the army invaded Korea.

sentences.zh: 叙功，封固山貝子。

translations.literal: Merit was assessed, and he was enfeoffed as gushan beizi.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as gushan beizi.

sentences.zh: 四年，坐受外籓蒙古賄，削爵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, for accepting bribes from outer vassal Mongols, his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was stripped of rank for taking bribes from Mongol tributaries.

sentences.zh: 尋復封輔國公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again enfeoffed as duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as duke who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 七年，伐明，敗明總兵白騰蛟等於薊州，克其城。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on an expedition against the Ming, he defeated Ming commander-in-chief Bai Tengjiao and others at Jizhou and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, campaigning against the Ming, he routed Ming commander Bai Tengjiao at Jizhou and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 八年，代戍錦州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he replaced the garrison at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took over the Jinzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 十二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，追封諡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 費揚武子七，有爵者三：尚善、傅喇塔、努賽。

translations.literal: Feiyangwu had seven sons; three held noble ranks: Shangshan, Fulata, and Nusai.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyangwu had seven sons, three of whom held titles: Shangshan, Fulata, and Nusai.

sentences.zh: 努賽封貝子，諡悼哀。

translations.literal: Nusai was enfeoffed as beizi and given the posthumous title Mournful Lament.
translations.idiomatic: Nusai was made beizi and posthumously titled Mournful Lament.

sentences.zh: 尚善，初襲輔國公。

translations.literal: Shangshan first succeeded as duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: Shangshan first inherited as duke who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，進貝子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was promoted to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he was raised to beizi.

sentences.zh: 二年，從多鐸南征擊李自成，敵以騎兵三百沖我師，尚善擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Dodo south to attack Li Zicheng; the enemy sent three hundred cavalry to charge our army, and Shangshan defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he followed Dodo south against Li Zicheng; when three hundred enemy horsemen charged the army, Shangshan beat them back.

sentences.zh: 平河南，下江南，並有功，賜圓補紗衣一襲、金百、銀五千、鞍馬一。

translations.literal: Pacifying Henan and descending on Jiangnan, he had merit in both; he was granted one suit of round-collared gauze clothing, one hundred taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, and one saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Henan and conquer Jiangnan, earning rewards of a round-collared gauze robe, a hundred taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 五年，戍大同。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he garrisoned Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he garrisoned Datong.

sentences.zh: 六年，進貝勒，掌理籓院，為議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to beile, took charge of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and became a deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was raised to beile, put in charge of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and made a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從多尼征雲南。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Duoni in the expedition against Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he joined Duoni's Yunnan campaign.

sentences.zh: 明桂王由榔奔永昌，尚善進鎮南州，破其將白文選于玉龍關，渡瀾滄江，下永昌，由榔先遁，乘勝取騰越，進南甸，至孟村而還。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui, Youlang, fled to Yongchang; Shangshan advanced to Zhennan Prefecture, defeated his general Bai Wenxuan at Yulong Pass, crossed the Lancang River, took Yongchang; Youlang fled first; following victory he took Tengyue, advanced to Nandian, and returned from Mengcun.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming Prince of Gui, Youlang, fled to Yongchang, Shangshan pushed into Zhennan Prefecture, routed Bai Wenxuan at Yulong Pass, crossed the Lancang, and took Yongchang. Youlang escaped ahead of him; Shangshan then seized Tengyue, pushed to Nandian, and withdrew from Mengcun.

sentences.zh: 十六年，賜蟒袍一、玲瓏刀一、鞍馬一。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was granted one python robe, one exquisite knife, and one saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he received a python robe, an exquisite knife, and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 十七年，追論尚善撤永昌守兵致軍士入城傷人罪，降貝子。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, on retrospective review of Shangshan's withdrawal of the Yongchang garrison, which had led soldiers entering the city to injure people, he was reduced to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was demoted to beizi on retrospective review of his withdrawal of the Yongchang garrison, which had allowed troops entering the city to harm civilians.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，復爵，任右宗正。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi his rank was restored, and he was appointed right director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 his rank was restored and he was named right director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 以疾罷。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his retirement.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 授安遠靖寇大將軍，率師之岳州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant and Quells Bandits, and led an army to Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant and Quells Bandits and marched on Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 尚善至軍，移書三桂曰：「王以亡國餘生，乞師我朝，殄殲賊寇，雪國恥，復父仇，蒙恩眷禮，列爵分籓，富貴榮寵，迄今三十餘年矣；

translations.literal: When Shangshan reached the army, he sent Wu Sangui a letter saying: "Your Highness, as a survivor of a fallen state, begged our dynasty for troops, destroyed the bandits, wiped away the national shame, and avenged your father; you received imperial favor and courtesies, were enfeoffed with a noble rank and granted a fief, and have enjoyed wealth, honors, and glory for more than thirty years now;
translations.idiomatic: When Shangshan reached the front, he wrote Wu Sangui: "Your Highness, a remnant of a fallen dynasty, begged our court for arms, helped destroy the bandits, avenged your father, and wiped away national disgrace. You were showered with imperial favor, enfeoffed, and granted a fief; for more than thirty years you have lived in wealth and honor—

sentences.zh: 而晚節末路，自取顛覆，竊為王不解也。

translations.literal: yet in your closing years you have brought ruin upon yourself—I truly cannot understand Your Highness's reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: yet in your last years you have chosen self-destruction. I confess I cannot fathom your reasoning.

sentences.zh: 王今藉口興復明室，曩者大兵入關，不聞請立明裔；

translations.literal: You now use reviving the Ming as your pretext; yet when our great army entered the Pass, we heard no request to install a Ming scion;
translations.idiomatic: You now claim to restore the Ming, yet when our armies entered the Pass no one asked that a Ming heir be enthroned;

sentences.zh: 天下大定，猶為我計除後患，翦滅明宗，安在其為故主效忠哉？

translations.literal: when the realm was largely pacified, you still helped us eliminate lingering threats and exterminate the Ming imperial line—where then was loyalty to your former master?
translations.idiomatic: when the realm was settled you still helped us root out the Ming line—where was loyalty to your old sovereign then?

sentences.zh: 將為子孫創大業，則公主、額駙入滇之時，何不即萌反側？

translations.literal: If you sought to build a great enterprise for your descendants, when the princess and the imperial son-in-law entered Yunnan, why did you not then harbor rebellious intent?
translations.idiomatic: If you meant to build an empire for your sons, why did you not rebel when the princess and her consort entered Yunnan?

sentences.zh: 至遣子入侍，乃復稱兵，以陷子於戮，可謂慈乎？

translations.literal: When you finally sent your son to serve at court, you again took up arms and thereby brought your son to execution—can this be called fatherly love?
translations.idiomatic: You then sent your son to serve at court, only to take up arms again and bring him to the execution ground—is that filial love toward a child?

sentences.zh: 若謂光耀前人，則王之投誠也，祖考皆膺封錫，今則墳塋毀棄，骸骨遺于道路，可謂孝乎？

translations.literal: If you claim to bring glory to your forebears, when you submitted in good faith your ancestors received enfeoffment and rewards; now their tombs are destroyed and their bones lie abandoned on the roads—can this be called filial piety?
translations.idiomatic: If you claim to honor your ancestors, your submission once won them titles and rewards; now their graves are desecrated and their bones lie on the roads—is that filial piety?

sentences.zh: 為人臣僕，身事兩朝，而未嘗忠於一主，可謂義乎？

translations.literal: As a subject and servant, you have served two dynasties yet been loyal to neither—can this be called righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: As a subject you have served two dynasties and been faithful to neither—is that righteousness?

sentences.zh: 躬蹈四罪，而猶逞志角力，謬欲收拾人心，是厝薪於火而雲安，結巢於幕而雲固也。

translations.literal: Having yourself committed these four crimes, yet you still seek to match strength with us and foolishly hope to win men's hearts—is this not like piling firewood on a fire yet claiming all is safe, or building a nest on a curtain yet claiming it is secure?
translations.idiomatic: Guilty of all four sins, you still seek to test strength against us and imagine you can win hearts—like stacking firewood on a blaze and calling it safe, or weaving a nest in a tent flap and calling it firm.

sentences.zh: 聖朝寬大，如輸誠悔罪，應許自新，毋蹈公孫述、彭寵故轍，赤族湛身，為世大僇。」

translations.literal: Our sacred dynasty is magnanimous: if you submit in sincerity and repent, you may be granted renewal. Do not follow the old tracks of Gongsun Shu and Peng Chong, bringing extermination upon your clan and disgrace upon yourself as a great shame to the age."
translations.idiomatic: The court is merciful: sincere repentance may yet win pardon. Do not repeat the fate of Gongsun Shu and Peng Chong, who brought their clans to extinction and themselves to everlasting shame."

sentences.zh: 三桂得書，不報。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui received the letter and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui received the letter and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 尚善疏請發荊州綠營兵、京口沙唬船五十，進攻岳州。

translations.literal: Shangshan memorialized requesting that Jingzhou Green Standard troops and fifty Jingkou shahu boats be sent to attack Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shangshan asked that Jingzhou Green Standard troops and fifty Jingkou river boats be sent to assault Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遣舟師絕敵餉道。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he sent a naval force to cut the enemy's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he sent a fleet to sever the enemy supply line.

sentences.zh: 十五年，敗賊於洞庭，取君山，分兵助攻長沙。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he defeated the rebels at Dongting, took Junshan, and divided troops to assist in the attack on Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he routed the rebels at Dongting, seized Junshan, and detached forces to help besiege Changsha.

sentences.zh: 十六年四月，三桂奔衡州，復出湘潭，分遣其侵兩粵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year Wu Sangui fled to Hengzhou, then again came out at Xiangtan and sent detachments to invade the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year Wu Sangui fled to Hengzhou, then reappeared at Xiangtan and sent columns to ravage Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔責尚善師無功，令率所部駐長沙，而以岳樂統大軍取岳州。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year an edict rebuked Shangshan's army for achieving no merit, ordered him to lead his own troops to garrison Changsha, and had Yuele command the great army to take Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the emperor rebuked Shangshan for lack of results, kept him at Changsha with his own troops, and put Yuele in command of the main force for Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 尚善請率舟師克岳州自效，上從之。

translations.literal: Shangshan requested to lead the naval force to capture Yuezhou as proof of his service; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Shangshan offered to take Yuezhou with the fleet to redeem himself, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 三桂將杜輝等犯柳林嘴，師迎擊，舟師來會，合戰，輝敗走。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's general Du Hui and others attacked Liulinzui; the army met and attacked them; the naval force came to join; in combined battle Hui was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui's general Du Hui attacked Liulinzui, Shangshan's land and river forces joined battle and drove Hui off.

sentences.zh: 八月，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 十九年，追論退縮罪，削貝勒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, on retrospective review of the crime of shrinking back, he was stripped of beile rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was posthumously stripped of beile rank for having held back in battle.

sentences.zh: 聖祖念尚善舊勞，授其子門度輔國公，世襲。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzu, remembering Shangshan's old service, appointed his son Mendu duke who assists the state, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Shangshan's earlier service, Kangxi granted his son Mendu a hereditary dukedom who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 惠獻貝子傅喇塔，費揚武第四子。

translations.literal: Fulata, Beizi of Gracious Offering, was the fourth son of Feiyangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Fulata, Beizi of Gracious Offering, was Feiyangwu's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初封輔國公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made duke who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，從勒克德渾徇湖廣，有功，賜金五十、銀千。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he followed Lekdehun in operations through Huguang and had merit; he was granted fifty taels of gold and a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he followed Lekdehun through Huguang with distinction and received fifty taels of gold and a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五年，復征湖廣，逐敵至廣西，賜銀六百。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again campaigned in Huguang, pursued the enemy to Guangxi, and was granted six hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he campaigned again in Huguang, chased the enemy into Guangxi, and received six hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 六年，進貝子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was raised to beizi.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以朝參失儀，降輔國公。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, for impropriety at court audience, he was reduced to duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was demoted to duke who assists the state for a breach of court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復爵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year his rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，耿精忠反，授甯海將軍，佐康親王傑書討之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, when Geng Jingzhong rebelled, he was appointed general of Ninghai and assisted Prince Kang Jieshu in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13, when Geng Jingzhong rebelled, he was named general of Ninghai and served under Prince Kang Jieshu in the suppression.

sentences.zh: 師至浙江，溫州、處州皆陷。

translations.literal: When the army reached Zhejiang, Wenzhou and Chuzhou had both fallen.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the army reached Zhejiang, Wenzhou and Chuzhou had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 傅喇塔師進台州，戰黃瑞山，擊斬精忠將陳鵬等，復破敵天臺紫雲山。

translations.literal: Fulata's army advanced to Taizhou; at Huangrui Mountain they fought, beheaded Jingzhong's general Chen Peng and others, and again defeated the enemy at Tiantai Ziyun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Fulata pushed into Taizhou, killed Jingzhong's general Chen Peng at Huangrui Mountain, and routed the enemy again at Tiantai's Ziyun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十四年，精忠將曾養性再犯台州，師自仙居襲其後，破之，乘勝圍黃岩，養性遁，城降。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Jingzhong's general Zeng Yangxing again attacked Taizhou; the army struck from behind via Xianju, defeated him, followed victory to besiege Huangyan; Yangxing fled and the city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when Zeng Yangxing attacked Taizhou again, Fulata struck from the rear through Xianju, defeated him, and besieged Huangyan until Yangxing fled and the city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 先後復太平、樂清、青田諸縣，進攻溫州，破敵南江。

translations.literal: In succession he recovered Taiping, Yueqing, Qingtian, and other counties, advanced to attack Wenzhou, and defeated the enemy at Nanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then retook Taiping, Yueqing, Qingtian, and other counties, advanced on Wenzhou, and defeated the enemy at Nanjiang.

sentences.zh: 十五年，精忠兵四萬水陸來犯，師分路迎擊，斬其將三百、兵二萬有奇。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Jingzhong's army of forty thousand came to attack by land and water; the army met them on divided routes, beheading three hundred of their generals and more than twenty thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year forty thousand of Jingzhong's troops attacked by land and water; Fulata met them on several fronts, killing three hundred officers and more than twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 初，傅喇塔之攻溫州也，以待紅衣炮為辭，繼言須戰船，傑書疏聞。

translations.literal: At first, when Fulata attacked Wenzhou, he pleaded that he was waiting for red-barrel cannon; afterward he said he needed war boats; Jieshu memorialized to report this.
translations.idiomatic: At first Fulata claimed he was waiting for red-barrel cannon before assaulting Wenzhou; later he said he needed war junks. Jieshu reported the shifting excuses to court.

sentences.zh: 上責其言先後歧，命剋期取溫州。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for contradictory statements and ordered that Wenzhou be taken by a fixed deadline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked the inconsistency and set a firm deadline for taking Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 傅喇塔疏言：「臣奉康親王檄催，心思皇惑，語言違謬。

translations.literal: Fulata memorialized: "I received Prince Kang's dispatch urging me on, and my mind was troubled and confused; my words were mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Fulata wrote: "Prince Kang's repeated orders have left me anxious and confused, and my words have gone astray.

sentences.zh: 臣前駐台州，王云：『待破台州，進福建。』

translations.literal: When I was stationed at Taizhou, Your Highness said: 'Wait until Taizhou is taken, then advance into Fujian.'
translations.idiomatic: When I held Taizhou, Your Highness said, 'After Taizhou falls, advance into Fujian.'

sentences.zh: 臣得黃岩，又云：『必取溫州。』

translations.literal: When I obtained Huangyan, you again said: 'Wenzhou must be taken.'
translations.idiomatic: After I took Huangyan, you said, 'Wenzhou must be taken first.'

sentences.zh: 以是責臣，臣將無辭。

translations.literal: To blame me on this account, I would have no words in reply.
translations.idiomatic: On those grounds alone I could offer no defense.

sentences.zh: 今蒙恩刻期下溫州，敢不戮力，但環溫州皆水，我軍不能猝入。」

translations.literal: Now, receiving the grace of a fixed deadline for Wenzhou, I dare not fail to exert my strength, but all around Wenzhou is water and our army cannot enter suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the court has set a deadline for Wenzhou, I will strive with all my strength; yet Wenzhou is ringed by water and our troops cannot rush in.

sentences.zh: 上命康親王留兵圍溫州，而趣傅喇塔率師自衢州規福建。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Prince Kang to leave troops to besiege Wenzhou and urged Fulata to lead an army from Quzhou toward Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince Kang to keep troops besieging Wenzhou while Fulata marched from Quzhou toward Fujian.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「王、貝子皆朕懿親，受命討賊，師克在和，宜同心合力，以奏膚功。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Prince and beizi are both my close kinsmen; charged with suppressing rebels, victory in the army depends on harmony—you should unite your hearts and combine your strength to achieve full merit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote: "You are both my close kinsmen, charged with crushing rebellion. Victory depends on unity—work together in full concert."

sentences.zh: 於是傅喇塔亦留兵圍溫州，而自率師攻處州，溯江抵得勝山。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fulata also left troops to besiege Wenzhou and personally led an army to attack Chuzhou, going upriver to Desheng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Fulata likewise left a siege force at Wenzhou and personally led troops against Chuzhou, advancing upriver to Desheng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 養性等以數百艘泊江中，復立兩營對江及得勝山下古溪，阻我師。

translations.literal: Yangxing and others moored several hundred boats in the river and again established two camps opposite the river and at Guxi below Desheng Mountain, blocking our army.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing anchored hundreds of boats in the river and built two camps on the far bank and at Guxi below Desheng Mountain to block the advance.

sentences.zh: 傅喇塔遣攻古溪，伏林中，敵敗，伏起截殺，併發炮碎敵舟及對江營。

translations.literal: Fulata sent troops to attack Guxi; they lay in ambush in the forest; when the enemy was defeated the ambush rose to intercept and kill; cannon were also fired, shattering enemy boats and the camp across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Fulata sent men against Guxi with troops hidden in the woods; when the enemy broke, the ambush cut them down while cannon fire smashed their boats and the camp across the river.

sentences.zh: 師進次溫溪渡口，敗精忠將馬成龍。

translations.literal: The army advanced to Wenxi Ford, defeated Jingzhong's general Ma Chenglong.
translations.idiomatic: The army moved to Wenxi Ford and defeated Jingzhong's general Ma Chenglong.

sentences.zh: 尋會傑書師於衢州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he joined Jieshu's army at Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Jieshu at Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 精忠兵屯雲和石塘嶺，擊之，破其壘二十八，克雲和。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's troops were encamped at Yunhe Shitang Ridge; they were attacked, twenty-eight of their strongpoints were broken, and Yunhe was taken.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunhe's Shitang Ridge they attacked Jingzhong's encampment, stormed twenty-eight positions, and captured Yunhe.

sentences.zh: 九月，師入福建，精忠降。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army entered Fujian and Jingzhong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army entered Fujian and Jingzhong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 浙江諸寇悉平。

translations.literal: All the bandits in Zhejiang were completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces throughout Zhejiang were fully suppressed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，賜祭奠，諡惠獻。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, libations were granted and he was given the posthumous title Gracious Offering.
translations.idiomatic: When his body was returned, the court granted funeral honors and the posthumous title Gracious Offering.

sentences.zh: 子富善，仍襲貝子。

translations.literal: His son Fushan still succeeded as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fushan inherited as beizi.

sentences.zh: 授左宗人。

translations.literal: He was appointed left director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 以病解任。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to resign.

sentences.zh: 諭責富善乖亂，奪爵。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Fushan for disorderly conduct and stripped his rank.
translations.idiomatic: The court rebuked Fushan for misconduct and stripped his title.

sentences.zh: 弟福存，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fucun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fucun inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 卒，子德普，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Depu succeeded as duke who stabilizes the state.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Depu inherited as duke who stabilizes the state.

sentences.zh: 授左宗人。

translations.literal: He was appointed left director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 卒，子恆魯，襲輔國公。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Henglu succeeded as duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Henglu inherited as duke who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 事高宗，曆工部侍郎、左宗人，綏遠城、盛京將軍，授內大臣。

translations.literal: Serving Emperor Gaozong, he successively held the posts of vice minister of Works, left director of the Imperial Clan Court, general of Suiyuan City and Mukden, and was appointed Inner Court minister.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he served as vice minister of Works, left director of the Imperial Clan Court, general of Suiyuan and Mukden, and Inner Court minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡恭懿。

translations.literal: When he died, he was given the posthumous title Reverent and Gracious.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the posthumous title Reverent and Gracious.

sentences.zh: 子興兆，襲輔國公。

translations.literal: His son Xingzhao succeeded as duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingzhao inherited as duke who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 事高宗，從征金川，為領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Serving Emperor Gaozong, he followed the campaign against Jinchuan as a leading commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he joined the Jinchuan campaign as a leading commander.

sentences.zh: 曆右宗人、荊州將軍。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of right director of the Imperial Clan Court and general of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as right director of the Imperial Clan Court and general of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 攻當噶拉、得黑、絨布寨、卡卡角諸地，有功。

translations.literal: Attacking Dangala, Dehei, Rongbu Stockade, Kaka Corner, and other places, he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Dangala, Dehei, Rongbu Stockade, Kaka Corner, and elsewhere with distinction.

sentences.zh: 金川平，畫像紫光閣。

translations.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinchuan was pacified, his portrait was hung in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 曆西安、綏遠城將軍。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of general of Xi'an and Suiyuan City.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as general of Xi'an and Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪官。

translations.literal: For an offense he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Misconduct cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 復授荊州將軍。

translations.literal: He was again appointed general of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as general of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 苗石柳鄧、吳半生、吳八月等為亂，與提督花連布擊吳半生，降；

translations.literal: The Miao Shi Liudeng, Wu Bansheng, Wu Bayue, and others raised rebellion; together with provincial commander Hua Lianbu he attacked Wu Bansheng, who surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao leaders Shi Liudeng, Wu Bansheng, and Wu Bayue rebelled, he joined provincial commander Hua Lianbu against Wu Bansheng, who submitted;

sentences.zh: 與內大臣額勒登保等擊吳八月，復擊石柳鄧，殲焉：屢荷恩賚。

translations.literal: together with Inner Court minister Eledengbao and others he attacked Wu Bayue, again attacked Shi Liudeng, and destroyed them: repeatedly he received imperial rewards.
translations.idiomatic: with Inner Court minister Eledengbao he defeated Wu Bayue, then crushed Shi Liudeng, earning repeated imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，討教匪姚之富、齊王氏等，師久無功，奪官，戍烏魯木齊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing, in suppressing the sect rebels Yao Zhifu, Qi Wangshi, and others, the army was long without success; he was stripped of office and banished to Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing, while campaigning against the White Lotus rebels Yao Zhifu and Qi Wangshi, prolonged failure brought dismissal and exile to Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 復授侍衛，駐和闐、塔爾巴哈台。

translations.literal: He was again appointed bodyguard and garrisoned Khotan and Tarbagatai.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as an imperial guardsman and posted to Khotan and Tarbagatai.

sentences.zh: 坐事，復奪官。

translations.literal: For an offense he was again stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Further misconduct cost him his post again.

sentences.zh: 子孫仍以輔國公世襲，錄傅喇塔功也。

translations.literal: His descendants still hereditarily held the title duke who assists the state, in record of Fulata's merit.
translations.idiomatic: His line still held the hereditary dukedom who assists the state in remembrance of Fulata's service.

sentences.zh: 舒爾哈齊諸孫，劄喀納、屯齊、洛托皆有功，受封。

translations.literal: Among Shu'erhachi's grandsons, Zhakana, Tunqi, and Luotuo all had merit and received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shu'erhachi's grandsons, Zhakana, Tunqi, and Luotuo all served with distinction and received titles.

sentences.zh: 劄喀納，扎薩克圖子。

translations.literal: Zhakana was the son of Zhasaketu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhakana was Zhasaketu's son.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年八月，睿親王多爾袞率師伐明，毀邊牆，至涿州，分軍八道入。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Chongde, Prince Regent Dorgon led an army against the Ming, destroyed the border wall, reached Zhuozhou, and divided the army into eight routes to enter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chongde 3, Prince Regent Dorgon invaded the Ming, breached the border wall, reached Zhuozhou, and sent eight columns into China.

sentences.zh: 劄喀納趨臨清州，渡運河，破濟南，還破天津衛，所向有功。

translations.literal: Zhakana hastened to Linqing Prefecture, crossed the Grand Canal, took Jinan, returned and broke Tianjin Guard, and wherever he went had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhakana raced to Linqing, crossed the Grand Canal, captured Jinan, turned back to smash Tianjin Guard, and won success wherever he marched.

sentences.zh: 四年，師還，賜駝馬各一、銀二千，封鎮國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the army returned, each was granted one camel and horse and two thousand taels of silver; he was enfeoffed as duke who stabilizes the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned in the fourth year he received a camel, a horse, and two thousand taels of silver, and was enfeoffed duke who stabilizes the state.

sentences.zh: 上命追蒙古、漢人之逃亡者，劄喀納以泥淖，不追而還，降輔國公。

translations.literal: The ruler ordered pursuit of fleeing Mongols and Han; Zhakana, because of mud and marsh, did not pursue and returned, and was reduced to duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to pursue fleeing Mongols and Han, Zhakana turned back because of marshland and was demoted to duke who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 六年，從上攻錦州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the ruler in attacking Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the siege of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 明總督洪承疇以兵犯鑲紅旗營，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Ming governor-general Hong Chengchou came with troops to attack the Bordered Red Banner camp; they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming governor-general Hong Chengchou attacked the Bordered Red Banner camp, Zhakana defeated him.

sentences.zh: 罷戰，敵襲我後，距百步而近，劄喀納奮力轉戰，敵驚遁。

translations.literal: When fighting ceased, the enemy raided our rear; within a hundred paces they drew near; Zhakana fought fiercely in a turning battle, and the enemy fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle the enemy struck the rear within a hundred paces; Zhakana wheeled and fought until they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 復偕輔國公費揚武，追擊明將吳三桂、白廣恩、王樸等於塔山。

translations.literal: Again together with Duke Who Assists the State Feiyangwu, he pursued Ming generals Wu Sangui, Bai Guangen, Wang Pu, and others at Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: With Duke Feiyangwu he then pursued Wu Sangui, Bai Guangen, Wang Pu, and other Ming generals to Tashan.

sentences.zh: 七年，戍錦州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he garrisoned Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he garrisoned Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 追論敏惠恭和元妃喪時劄喀納從武英郡王阿濟格歌舞為樂，大不敬，削爵，黜宗籍，幽禁。

translations.literal: On retrospective review, during the mourning for Primary Consort Minhui Gonghe it was charged that Zhakana followed Prince Wu Ying Ajige in song and dance for pleasure—great disrespect; his rank was reduced, he was struck from the clan register, and confined.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was judged that during mourning for Primary Consort Minhui Gonghe, Zhakana had joined Prince Wu Ying Ajige in song and dance—gross disrespect. He was stripped of rank, removed from the clan register, and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 順治初，釋之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was released.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shunzhi he was freed.

sentences.zh: 從多爾袞敗李自成，復宗籍，授輔國公品級。

translations.literal: Following Dorgon in defeating Li Zicheng, he was restored to the clan register and granted the rank of duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: After helping Dorgon defeat Li Zicheng, he was restored to the clan register at duke-who-assists-the-state rank.

sentences.zh: 偕鎮國公傅勒赫戍江南，復從平南大將軍勒克德渾徇湖廣。

translations.literal: Together with Duke Who Stabilizes the State Fulehe he garrisoned Jiangnan, and again followed the Pacifier of the South Grand General Lekdehun in operations through Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: With Duke Fulehe he garrisoned Jiangnan, then joined Pacifier of the South Lekdehun in the Huguang campaign.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜金五十、銀千。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted fifty taels of gold and a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: On return he received fifty taels of gold and a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五年，從郡王瓦克達赴英親王阿濟格軍戍大同。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Prince Wakeda to Prince Ying Ajige's army garrisoning Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined Prince Wakeda at Prince Ying Ajige's Datong garrison.

sentences.zh: 六年，進貝子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was raised to beizi.

sentences.zh: 九年，從定遠大將軍尼堪征湖南，賜蟒衣、鞍馬、弓矢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant Nikan in the expedition against Hunan and was granted a python robe, saddle horse, and bow and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he joined Grand General Nikan in Hunan and received a python robe, saddle horse, and bow and arrows.

sentences.zh: 至衡州，尼堪戰歿，上以貝勒屯齊與劄喀納合領其軍。

translations.literal: At Hengzhou, Nikan died in battle; the emperor had Beile Tunqi and Zhakana jointly command his army.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengzhou Nikan was killed in action; the emperor put Beile Tunqi and Zhakana in joint command of his army.

sentences.zh: 敗明兵于周家坡。

translations.literal: They defeated Ming troops at Zhoujiapo.
translations.idiomatic: They routed Ming forces at Zhoujiapo.

sentences.zh: 十一年，追論衡州敗績罪，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on retrospective review of the defeat at Hengzhou, his rank was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was stripped of rank for the Hengzhou defeat.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復授輔國公品級。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was again granted the rank of duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was restored to duke-who-assists-the-state rank.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從定遠靖寇大將軍多尼徇雲南，克永昌。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant and Quells Bandits Duoni in operations through Yunnan and took Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he joined Grand General Duoni in Yunnan and captured Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 十六年閏三月，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month of the sixteenth year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp in the intercalary third month of the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子瑪喀納，襲。

translations.literal: His son Makana succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Makana inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 三等鎮國將軍品級屯齊，圖倫子。

translations.literal: Tunqi, of third-rank duke-who-stabilizes-the-state general rank, was the son of Tulun.
translations.idiomatic: Tunqi, a third-rank duke who stabilizes the state, was Tulun's son.

sentences.zh: 圖倫，舒爾哈齊第四子，追封貝勒，諡恪僖。

translations.literal: Tulun, the fourth son of Shu'erhachi, was posthumously enfeoffed as beile and given the posthumous title Reverent and Joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Tulun, Shu'erhachi's fourth son, was posthumously made beile with the title Reverent and Joyful.

sentences.zh: 屯齊，事太宗，從英親王阿濟格伐明，有功。

translations.literal: Tunqi served Taizong; following Prince Ying Ajige in an expedition against the Ming, he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tunqi served Taizong and distinguished himself on Prince Ying Ajige's Ming campaigns.

sentences.zh: 從鄭親王濟爾哈朗略錦州、松山、杏山，九戰九勝。

translations.literal: Following Prince of Zheng Jirhalang in raiding Jinzhou, Songshan, and Xingshan, he fought nine battles and won nine victories.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince of Zheng Jirhalang he raided Jinzhou, Songshan, and Xingshan, winning nine battles in nine engagements.

sentences.zh: 屯齊受創，加賜銀百，封輔國公。

translations.literal: Tunqi was wounded; an additional grant of a hundred taels of silver was given, and he was enfeoffed as duke who assists the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded in service, he received an extra hundred taels of silver and was enfeoffed duke who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 五年，從睿親王多爾袞圍錦州，明兵夜襲鑲藍旗營，擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Prince Regent Dorgon in besieging Jinzhou; Ming troops raided the Bordered Blue Banner camp by night and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, during Dorgon's siege of Jinzhou, he repulsed a night attack on the Bordered Blue Banner camp.

sentences.zh: 坐不臨城及私遣兵還，議削爵，命罰銀千。

translations.literal: For not approaching the city wall and privately sending troops back, deprivation of rank was discussed; he was ordered to pay a fine of a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Because he failed to press the walls and sent troops home without leave, officials debated stripping his rank; he was fined a thousand taels of silver instead.

sentences.zh: 六年，從上攻錦州、塔山，敗明兵，復從多爾袞圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the ruler in attacking Jinzhou and Tashan, defeated Ming troops, and again followed Dorgon in besieging Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he fought at Jinzhou and Tashan, defeated Ming forces, and returned to the Jinzhou siege under Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，進貝子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was promoted to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he was raised to beizi.

sentences.zh: 尋從豫親王多鐸破流寇，平陝西、河南並有功，賜圓補紗衣一襲。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Prince Yu Dodo in breaking the roving bandits, pacifying Shaanxi and Henan with joint merit, and was granted one suit of round-collared gauze clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Prince Yu Dodo against the roving rebels, helped pacify Shaanxi and Henan, and received a round-collared gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 從多鐸下江寧，明福王由崧走太平，與貝勒尼堪追至蕪湖，獲之。

translations.literal: Following Dodo in descending on Jiangning, the Ming Prince of Fu, Yousong, fled to Taiping; together with Beile Nikan he pursued to Wuhu and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dodo marched on Jiangning, the Ming Prince of Fu, Yousong, fled to Taiping; Tunqi and Beile Nikan chased him to Wuhu and took him.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜金百、銀五千、鞍馬一，授鑲藍旗滿洲固山額真。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted a hundred taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, and one saddle horse, and was appointed gushan ejen of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: On return he received a hundred taels of gold, five thousand of silver, a saddle horse, and appointment as gushan ejen of the Bordered Blue Manchu Banner.

sentences.zh: 三年，從肅親王豪格西征，破賀珍，解漢中圍。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Su Hooge on the western expedition, defeated He Zhen, and relieved the siege of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined Prince Su Hooge in the west, defeated He Zhen, and lifted the siege of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 會一隻虎、孫守法陷興安，進師漢陰，擊走之。

translations.literal: When Yizhihu and Sun Shoufa seized Xing'an, the army advanced to Hanyin and attacked, driving them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhihu and Sun Shoufa took Xing'an, he advanced to Hanyin and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 五年，陝西回亂，命為平西大將軍，率師討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with the Hui rebellion in Shaanxi, he was appointed Grand General Who Pacifies the West and led an army to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, amid the Hui uprising in Shaanxi, he was named Grand General Who Pacifies the West and sent to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 總督孟喬芳已擊斬回酋米喇印、丁國棟等，還赴英親王阿濟格軍，戍大同。

translations.literal: Governor-general Meng Qiaofang had already attacked and beheaded the Hui chieftains Mila Yin, Ding Guodong, and others; he returned to join Prince Ying Ajige's army garrisoning Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Meng Qiaofang had already killed the Hui leaders Mila Yin and Ding Guodong; Tunqi then rejoined Prince Ying Ajige's Datong garrison.

sentences.zh: 六年，進貝勒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was raised to beile.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠將孫可望、李定國等降于明桂王由榔，擾湖南。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong's generals Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and others surrendered to the Ming Prince of Gui, Youlang, and harassed Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong's generals Sun Kewang and Li Dingguo submitted to the Ming Prince of Gui, Youlang, and ravaged Hunan.

sentences.zh: 九年，屯齊從定遠大將軍尼堪南征。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Tunqi followed Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant Nikan on the southern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Tunqi joined Grand General Nikan's southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 尼堪戰歿，以屯齊代將。

translations.literal: Nikan died in battle; Tunqi replaced him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Nikan was killed, Tunqi took command in his place.

sentences.zh: 時定國及別將馬進忠率兵四萬餘，屯永州。

translations.literal: At that time Dingguo and the separate general Ma Jinzhong led more than forty thousand troops encamped at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo and the separate commander Ma Jinzhong then held Yongzhou with more than forty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 定國聞師至，度龍虎關先遁。

translations.literal: When Dingguo heard the army had arrived, he crossed Longhu Pass first and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the army's approach, Dingguo slipped away through Longhu Pass.

sentences.zh: 可望在靖州，別將馮雙禮在武岡。

translations.literal: Kewang was at Jingzhou; the separate general Feng Shuangli was at Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang was at Jingzhou; the separate commander Feng Shuangli at Wugang.

sentences.zh: 屯齊進師寶慶，至周家坡，雙禮、進忠據險抗我師，會暮天雨，列陣相拒。

translations.literal: Tunqi advanced the army to Baoqing, reaching Zhoujiapo; Shuangli and Jinzhong held the heights to resist our army; at evening it rained and the armies drew up facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Tunqi marched on Baoqing to Zhoujiapo, where Shuangli and Jinzhong held the high ground. At dusk rain fell and the two armies faced each other across the field.

sentences.zh: 其夜可望自寶慶以兵來會，衆號十萬，屯齊分兵縱擊，大破之。

translations.literal: That night Kewang came from Baoqing with troops to join them; the multitude was proclaimed at one hundred thousand; Tunqi divided troops to strike broadly and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: That night Sun Kewang marched from Baoqing with reinforcements; their force was said to reach one hundred thousand. Tunqi split his command and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 十一年，追坐衡州敗績，削爵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on retrospective review of the defeat at Hengzhou, his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was stripped of rank for the Hengzhou defeat.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授鎮國公品級。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was granted the rank of duke who stabilizes the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was restored to duke-who-stabilizes-the-state rank.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從多尼徇雲南，定國挾由榔奔永昌，降其餘衆。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Duoni in operations through Yunnan; Dingguo took Youlang and fled to Yongchang, and the remaining troops surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he joined Duoni in Yunnan; Li Dingguo fled to Yongchang with Youlang, and the rest submitted.

sentences.zh: 還。

translations.literal: He returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 2.

sentences.zh: 子溫齊，初封貝子，授右宗人、鑲藍旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: His son Wenqi was first enfeoffed as beizi and appointed right director of the Imperial Clan Court and lieutenant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenqi was first made beizi, then served as right director of the Imperial Clan Court and lieutenant-general of the Bordered Blue Manchu Banner.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，上命定西大將軍董額自陝西徇四川，溫齊從。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, the emperor ordered Grand General Who Pacifies the West Dong'e to conduct operations through Sichuan from Shaanxi; Wenqi followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, the emperor sent Grand General Dong'e from Shaanxi into Sichuan; Wenqi went with him.

sentences.zh: 陝西提督王輔臣叛應三桂，師駐漢中。

translations.literal: Shaanxi provincial commander Wang Fuchen rebelled in response to Wu Sangui; the army halted at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi commander Wang Fuchen joined Wu Sangui, the army halted at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進次隴州，克仙逸、關山二關，復秦州禮縣，逐敵至西和，清水、伏羌並下。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he advanced to Longzhou, took the two passes Xianyi and Guanshan, recovered Qinzhou and Li County, pursued the enemy to Xihe, and took Qingshui and Fugiang together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he advanced to Longzhou, seized the Xianyi and Guanshan passes, retook Qinzhou and Li County, pursued the enemy to Xihe, and captured Qingshui and Fugiang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔責董額師久無功，溫齊亦坐降輔國公，奪官。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year an edict rebuked Dong'e's army for long being without success; Wenqi also was reduced to duke who assists the state and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the emperor rebuked Dong'e for lack of progress; Wenqi was demoted to duke who assists the state and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三桂陷湖南，安遠靖寇大將軍尚善規岳州，上發禁旅，命溫齊率以往，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui seized Hunan, Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant and Quells Bandits Shangshan planned for Yuezhou; the emperor sent the Forbidden Army and ordered Wenqi to lead them there and assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui took Hunan, Shangshan turned toward Yuezhou; the emperor sent the Forbidden Army under Wenqi to assist.

sentences.zh: 十七年，敗賊于柳林嘴、於君山、于陸石口，進克岳州。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he defeated the rebels at Liulinzui, at Junshan, and at Lushikou, advanced and took Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he won victories at Liulinzui, Junshan, and Lushikou and captured Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，溫齊追三桂將吳應麒，以未攜爨具，引還，且妄報陣斬五千餘級。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Wenqi pursued Wu Sangui's general Wu Yingqi; because he had not brought cooking utensils, he turned back, and moreover falsely reported that five thousand ranks had been beheaded in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Wenqi pursued Wu Yingqi but turned back for lack of camp gear and falsely claimed five thousand enemy killed.

sentences.zh: 時尚善已卒，察尼代將。

translations.literal: At that time Shangshan had already died; Chani replaced him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shangshan had died and Chani had taken command.

sentences.zh: 事聞，命察尼按鞫之，溫齊坐削爵。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor ordered Chani to investigate and try the case; Wenqi was stripped of rank for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Chani was ordered to investigate; Wenqi lost his title.

sentences.zh: 洛讬，寨桑武子。

translations.literal: Luotuo was the son of Zaisangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Luotuo was Zaisangwu's son.

sentences.zh: 寨桑武，舒爾哈齊第五子，追封貝勒，諡和惠。

translations.literal: Zaisangwu, the fifth son of Shu'erhachi, was posthumously enfeoffed as beile and given the posthumous title Harmonious and Gracious.
translations.idiomatic: Zaisangwu, Shu'erhachi's fifth son, was posthumously made beile with the title Harmonious and Gracious.

sentences.zh: 洛讬，天聰八年，從太宗伐明。

translations.literal: Luotuo, in the eighth year of Tiancong, followed Taizong in an expedition against the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 Luotuo joined Taizong's Ming campaign.

sentences.zh: 上駐師大同南山西岡，洛讬籍所俘以獻。

translations.literal: The ruler encamped the army on the western ridge of South Mountain at Datong; Luotuo registered the captives and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: When the army camped on Datong's South Mountain west ridge, Luotuo tallied the captives and presented them.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he was enfeoffed beizi.

sentences.zh: 從伐朝鮮，偕貝勒多鐸圍南漢山城。

translations.literal: Following the expedition against Korea, together with Beile Dodo he besieged Namhansanseong.
translations.idiomatic: On the Korean campaign he joined Beile Dodo in besieging Namhansanseong.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮將以八千人赴援，盡殲之；

translations.literal: Korean generals came with eight thousand men as relief; they were completely annihilated;
translations.idiomatic: An eight-thousand-man Korean relief force was wiped out;

sentences.zh: 又以五千人赴援，擊之，敗走。

translations.literal: again five thousand came as relief; they were attacked and fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: when five thousand more came, he attacked and routed them.

sentences.zh: 二年，與議政。

translations.literal: In the second year he joined deliberations in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he joined the deliberative council.

sentences.zh: 四年，從英親王阿濟格圍塔山、連山。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Prince Ying Ajige in besieging Tashan and Lianshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined Prince Ying Ajige in the sieges of Tashan and Lianshan.

sentences.zh: 五年，從睿親王多爾袞屯田義州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Prince Regent Dorgon in garrison farming at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he garrison-farmed at Yizhou under Prince Regent Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 錦州兵夜襲我鑲藍旗營，與屯齊共擊敗之。

translations.literal: Jinzhou troops raided our Bordered Blue Banner camp by night; together with Tunqi they defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinzhou troops raided the Bordered Blue camp by night, he and Tunqi drove them off.

sentences.zh: 六年，坐圍錦州不臨城，且私遣兵還，議削爵，詔罰銀千。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, for not approaching the city in besieging Jinzhou and privately sending troops back, deprivation of rank was discussed; an edict ordered a fine of a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, for failing to press the Jinzhou walls and sending men home without leave, officials debated stripping his rank; he was fined a thousand taels instead.

sentences.zh: 上征松山，大破明總督洪承疇兵。

translations.literal: The ruler campaigned at Songshan and routed the army of Ming governor-general Hong Chengchou.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler fought at Songshan, Hong Chengchou's army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 洛讬橫擊潰兵於塔山，復圍錦州。

translations.literal: Luotuo struck the routed troops at Tashan crosswise and again besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luotuo cut across the fleeing Ming troops at Tashan and returned to the Jinzhou siege.

sentences.zh: 七年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗攻塔山，克之，授都察院承政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Prince of Zheng Jirhalang in attacking Tashan and took it; he was appointed censor-in-chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he helped Prince of Zheng Jirhalang take Tashan and was named censor-in-chief of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 偕博洛、尼堪駐錦州。

translations.literal: Together with Boluo and Nikan he garrisoned Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Boluo and Nikan he garrisoned Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，坐事，削爵，幽禁。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, for an offense, his rank was reduced and he was confined.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year misconduct cost him his title and brought imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 順治初，釋之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was released.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shunzhi he was freed.

sentences.zh: 八年，復封三等鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was again enfeoffed as third-rank duke who stabilizes the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was restored as a third-rank duke who stabilizes the state.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授鑲藍旗滿洲固山額真。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed gushan ejen of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became gushan ejen of the Bordered Blue Manchu Banner.

sentences.zh: 十四年，孫可望、李定國、馮雙禮等擾湖南，命為甯南靖寇將軍，駐防荊州，佐經略洪承疇討之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, Feng Shuangli, and others harassed Hunan; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Quells Bandits, garrisoned Jingzhou, and assisted Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, as Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and Feng Shuangli ravaged Hunan, he was named General Who Pacifies the South, posted at Jingzhou, and assigned to assist coordinator Hong Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 遣兵取心潭隘，斷巴東渡口，可望將趙世超、譚新傳、趙三才皆降。

translations.literal: He sent troops to take Xintan Pass, cut the Badong crossing, and Kewang's generals Zhao Shichao, Tan Xinchuan, and Zhao Sancai all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Xintan Pass, severed the Badong crossing, and Kewang's generals Zhao Shichao, Tan Xinchuan, and Zhao Sancai submitted.

sentences.zh: 俄，可望與定國內訌，戰不勝，亦來降。

translations.literal: Soon Kewang and Dingguo quarreled internally, were defeated in battle, and Kewang also came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kewang and Dingguo fell out, lost a battle, and Kewang surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 上命偕都統濟席哈自湖南進取貴州。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him together with lieutenant-general Jixihai to advance from Hunan and take Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him and Lieutenant-general Jixihai to advance from Hunan into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，與承疇會師常德，次辰州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he joined forces with Chengchou at Changde and halted at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he joined Chengchou at Changde and moved to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 復沅陵、瀘溪、麻陽、黔陽、溆浦諸縣，進次沅州。

translations.literal: He recovered Yuanling, Luxi, Mayang, Qianyang, and Xupu counties, and advanced to halt at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Yuanling, Luxi, Mayang, Qianyang, and Xupu, and advanced to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 檄偏沅巡撫袁廓宇徇靖州，屯鎮遠二十里山口以禦敵。

translations.literal: He issued a dispatch ordering Bian-Yuan governor Yuan Kuoyu to conduct operations through Jingzhou; troops were encamped twenty li from Zhenyuan at Shankou to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Bian-Yuan governor Yuan Kuoyu to operate through Jingzhou while his own force camped twenty li from Zhenyuan at Shankou to block the enemy.

sentences.zh: 雙禮部將馮天裕、閻廷桂等先後自平越降。

translations.literal: Shuangli's subordinate generals Feng Tianyu, Yan Tinggui, and others successively surrendered from Pingyue.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shuangli's officers Feng Tianyu and Yan Tinggui surrendered one after another from Pingyue.

sentences.zh: 四月，師至貴州，明將羅大順收潰卒襲新添衛，擊敗之，洛讬與承疇守貴陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the army reached Guizhou; the Ming general Luo Dashun gathered routed soldiers and raided Xintian Guard; they were defeated; Luotuo and Chengchou defended Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the army reached Guizhou; when Luo Dashun rallied broken troops against Xintian Guard they were beaten back, and Luotuo with Chengchou held Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，師還。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 叙功，加授拖沙喇哈番，進一等鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: Merit was assessed; he was additionally granted the rank of tošan bahan, and promoted to first-rank duke who stabilizes the state.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received the rank of tošan bahan and promotion to first-rank duke who stabilizes the state.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命為安南將軍，征鄭成功，大破之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed General of Annan and campaigned against Zheng Chenggong, routing him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, as General of Annan, he campaigned against Zheng Chenggong and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 十一月，還。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He returned in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 4.

sentences.zh: 子富達禮，襲拜他喇布勒哈番世職。

translations.literal: His son Fudali succeeded to the hereditary office of bataran bahan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fudali inherited the hereditary rank of bataran bahan.

sentences.zh: 旋改襲奉恩將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the succession was changed to recipient of imperial grace general.
translations.idiomatic: The line soon shifted to recipient of imperial grace general.

sentences.zh: 八年，進一等輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to first-rank assistant duke general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was raised to first-rank assistant duke general.

sentences.zh: 坐諂索額圖，為其從弟所訐，削爵。

translations.literal: For flattering Songgotu he was impeached by Songgotu's younger male cousin and stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery of Songgotu brought impeachment by Songgotu's cousin and loss of his title.

sentences.zh: 通達郡王雅爾哈齊，顯祖第四子，太祖同母弟。

translations.literal: Prince of Tongda Ya'erhaqi was the fourth son of Emperor Xian and the younger brother of the same mother as Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Tongda Ya'erhaqi was Emperor Xianzu's fourth son and Taizu's younger uterine brother.

sentences.zh: 其生平不著。

translations.literal: His life is not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: His life is not recorded in detail.

sentences.zh: 順治十年五月，追封諡，配享太廟。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title, with joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Shunzhi 10 he received posthumous enfeoffment and was granted joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 篤義剛果貝勒巴雅喇，顯祖第五子。

translations.literal: Bayala, Beile of Sincere Righteousness and Bold Achievement, was the fifth son of Emperor Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Bayala, Beile of Sincere Righteousness and Bold Achievement, was Emperor Xianzu's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 初授台吉。

translations.literal: He was first appointed taiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made taiji.

sentences.zh: 歲戊戌正月，太祖命偕褚英伐安楚拉庫路，夜取屯寨二十，降萬餘人，賜號卓禮克圖，譯言「篤義」。

translations.literal: In the first month of the year wuxu the Taizu ordered him together with Cuying to campaign against the Antuchalu route; by night they took twenty stockaded villages and reduced more than ten thousand people; he was granted the style Zhuolikeitu, translated as "sincere righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the wuxu year Taizu sent him with Cuying against the Antuchalu route; in a night assault they took twenty villages and subdued more than ten thousand people, earning the style Zhuolikeitu—"sincere righteousness."

sentences.zh: 歲丁未五月，伐東海窩集部，取赫席赫、鄂謨和蘇魯、佛訥赫托克索三路，俘二千人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the year dingwei he campaigned against the Eastern Sea Woji tribe, taking the three routes Hexihe, Emohesulu, and Fonehetuokesuo, and capturing two thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the dingwei year he attacked the Eastern Sea Woji, seized the Hexihe, Emohesulu, and Fonehetuokesuo routes, and took two thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 天命九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianming he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianming 9.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，追封諡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子拜音圖，事太宗，授三等昂邦章京、鑲黃旗固山額真。

translations.literal: His son Baiyintu served Taizong and was appointed third-rank angbang janggin and gushan ejen of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baiyintu served Taizong as third-rank angbang janggin and gushan ejen of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年五月，從武英郡王阿濟格略保定，攻安肅，克之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Chongde he followed Prince Wu Ying Ajige in raiding Baoding, attacked Ansu, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Chongde 1 he joined Prince Wu Ying Ajige in raiding Baoding, attacked Ansu, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 十月，獻所獲於篤恭殿，上以拜音圖戰不忘君，深嘉之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he presented what had been captured in the Hall of Reverent Respect; the ruler, because Baiyintu in battle did not forget his lord, deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he presented spoils in the Hall of Reverent Respect; the ruler praised him warmly for fighting without forgetting his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 從伐朝鮮，騎入城，收其輜重。

translations.literal: Following the expedition against Korea, he rode into the city and seized its baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: On the Korean campaign he rode into the city and seized its baggage.

sentences.zh: 三年，從睿親王多爾袞伐明，偕固山額真圖爾格敗敵董家口，毀邊牆入，克青山關下城。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Regent Dorgon in an expedition against the Ming; together with gushan ejen Turgene he defeated the enemy at Dongjiakou, destroyed the border wall to enter, and took the lower city of Qingshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined Dorgon's Ming invasion; with gushan ejen Turgene he routed the enemy at Dongjiakou, broke through the border wall, and took the lower town at Qingshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜音圖弟鞏阿岱從大軍圍錦州，臨陣退撓，下王大臣鞫其罪，拜音圖拂袖出，坐徇庇，論死，命奪爵職，罰鍰贖罪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Baiyintu's younger brother Gongadai followed the great army in besieging Jinzhou; at the battle line he shrank back; princes and ministers were ordered to try his crime; Baiyintu flung his sleeves and walked out; for favoring and shielding him, death was discussed; he was ordered to be stripped of rank and office and pay a fine to redeem the crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his brother Gongadai, besieging Jinzhou with the main army, hung back in battle; princes and ministers were ordered to judge him. Baiyintu stormed out in protest; charged with shielding him, he faced death but was stripped of rank and fined instead.

sentences.zh: 尋率師助多爾袞攻錦州，復偕多鐸圍松山。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he led troops to assist Dorgon in attacking Jinzhou, and again together with Dodo besieged Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led troops to help Dorgon at Jinzhou and joined Dodo in the Songshan siege.

sentences.zh: 七年，復授固山額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again appointed gushan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was restored as gushan ejen.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，從多鐸西征，敗敵潼關，封一等鎮國將軍，賜繡服一襲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he followed Dodo on the western expedition, defeated the enemy at Tong Pass, was enfeoffed as first-rank duke who stabilizes the state, and was granted one suit of embroidered clothing.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he followed Dodo west, routed the enemy at Tong Pass, was made first-rank duke who stabilizes the state, and received an embroidered robe.

sentences.zh: 復從南征，克揚州，又以舟師破其兵於江南岸，偕貝子博洛下杭州。

translations.literal: Again following the southern expedition, he took Yangzhou, and again with the naval force broke their army on the south bank of the Jiang; together with Beizi Boluo he descended on Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he took Yangzhou, smashed enemy forces on the south bank with the fleet, and with Beizi Boluo captured Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 叙功，賜金八十、銀四千、鞍馬一。

translations.literal: Merit was assessed; he was granted eighty taels of gold, four thousand taels of silver, and one saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received eighty taels of gold, four thousand of silver, and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 三年，授三等公。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made a third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 五年，進貝子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was raised to beizi.

sentences.zh: 從阿濟格戍大同。

translations.literal: He followed Ajige in garrisoning Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Datong under Ajige.

sentences.zh: 叛將薑瓖既死，餘黨猶分據郡邑。

translations.literal: After the rebel general Jiang Xiang died, the remnant bandits still held separate counties and districts.
translations.idiomatic: After rebel general Jiang Xiang's death, his followers still held towns across the region.

sentences.zh: 六年，拔沁州，復圍瓖將胡國鼎于潞安，殲其衆，進貝勒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he took Qin Prefecture, again besieged Jiang's general Hu Guoding at Lu'an, destroyed his force, and was promoted to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he seized Qin Prefecture, besieged Jiang's general Hu Guoding at Lu'an, destroyed his force, and was raised to beile.

sentences.zh: 鞏阿岱事多爾袞，最見信任，累進封貝子。

translations.literal: Gongadai served Dorgon and was most trusted; he was repeatedly promoted and enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: Gongadai served Dorgon and enjoyed his fullest trust, rising repeatedly to beizi.

sentences.zh: 多爾袞既薨，坐黨附罪，死。

translations.literal: After Dorgon died, for the crime of factional attachment he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After Dorgon's death he was executed for factional loyalty to him.

sentences.zh: 拜音圖亦牽連，削爵，幽禁，削宗籍。

translations.literal: Baiyintu was also implicated, stripped of rank, confined, and struck from the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyintu was implicated as well: stripped of rank, imprisoned, and removed from the clan register.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，仁宗命復宗籍，賜紅帶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing Emperor Renzong ordered restoration to the clan register and granted a red sash.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 Emperor Renzong restored the clan register and granted a red sash.

sentences.zh: 鞏阿岱裔孫伊裏布，自有傳。

translations.literal: Gongadai's descendant Yilibu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Gongadai's descendant Yilibu is treated in a separate biography.
